title: From Tables to Time: Extending TabPFN-v2 to Time Series Forecasting
summary: Recent progress in foundation models has enabled strong zero-shot performance for time series forecasting. In this work, we show that such capabilities can also emerge from tabular foundation models. We introduce TabPFN-TS, a simple method that treats forecasting as a tabular regression problem by combining lightweight temporal featurization with the pretrained TabPFN-v2. This formulation requires no time-series-specific pretraining and naturally supports both univariate and covariate-informed forecasting. Despite its compact size (11M parameters), TabPFN-TS achieves state-of-the-art performance on covariate-informed forecasting and competitive accuracy on univariate forecasting across the GIFT-Eval and fev-bench benchmarks. We further provide controlled analyses examining how the model interprets temporal structure, how featurization choices affect accuracy, and how forecasts change under alternative tabular backbones. Together, our results demonstrate that tabular foundation models--when paired with suitable temporal features--offer an efficient and versatile alternative for forecasting, bridging tabular and time-series learning within a unified framework. Code is available at https://github.com/PriorLabs/tabpfn-time-series.
core_methodology: The paper introduces TabPFN-TS, a method that treats time series forecasting as a tabular regression problem by combining lightweight temporal featurization with the pre-trained TabPFN-v2 model. This approach leverages tabular foundation models for time-series forecasting without requiring time-series-specific pre-training.
data_sources: The model is evaluated on the GIFT-Eval and fev-bench benchmarks, which are standard datasets for time series forecasting. These datasets likely include both univariate and covariate-informed forecasting tasks.
alpha_potential: TabPFN-TS demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on covariate-informed forecasting and competitive accuracy on univariate forecasting. Its ability to handle both types of forecasting tasks efficiently (with only 11M parameters) suggests potential for generating alpha in trading strategies that rely on time-series predictions, such as momentum or mean-reversion strategies.
title_cn: 从表格到时间：将TabPFN-v2扩展至时间序列预测
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种新型时间序列预测方法TabPFN-TS，通过轻量级时间特征化与预训练TabPFN-v2结合，将预测任务转化为表格回归问题。该方法在协变量预测任务中表现最优，在单变量预测中也具有竞争力。对于依赖时间序列预测的量化交易策略（如动量或均值回归）具有实际应用潜力，尤其是其高效的小模型特性（仅1100万参数）适合实时交易场景。

title: Average-reward reinforcement learning in semi-Markov decision processes via relative value iteration
summary: This paper applies the authors' recent results on asynchronous stochastic approximation (SA) in the Borkar-Meyn framework to reinforcement learning in average-reward semi-Markov decision processes (SMDPs). We establish the convergence of an asynchronous SA analogue of Schweitzer's classical relative value iteration algorithm, RVI Q-learning, for finite-space, weakly communicating SMDPs. In particular, we show that the algorithm converges almost surely to a compact, connected subset of solutions to the average-reward optimality equation, with convergence to a unique, sample path-dependent solution under additional stepsize and asynchrony conditions. Moreover, to make full use of the SA framework, we introduce new monotonicity conditions for estimating the optimal reward rate in RVI Q-learning. These conditions substantially expand the previously considered algorithmic framework and are addressed through novel arguments in the stability and convergence analysis of RVI Q-learning.
core_methodology: The paper presents an asynchronous stochastic approximation (SA) method for reinforcement learning in average-reward semi-Markov decision processes (SMDPs). It develops a relative value iteration (RVI) Q-learning algorithm for weakly communicating SMDPs, with guaranteed convergence to solutions of the average-reward optimality equation. The paper introduces novel monotonicity conditions for estimating the optimal reward rate to enhance stability and convergence.
data_sources: Theoretically, this method can be applied to any financial time-series data or market microstructure data where sequential decision-making is required. In finance, SMDPs can model trading environments with variable time intervals between decisions.
alpha_potential: The algorithm could potentially identify optimal trading strategies in market conditions where reward structures vary over time (e.g., different market regimes). The SMDP framework accommodates realistic trading scenarios where the time between decisions isn't fixed (unlike traditional MDPs). The proven convergence properties make this theoretically more robust than standard Q-learning for financial applications.
title_cn: 通过相对值迭代在半马尔可夫决策过程中实现平均奖励强化学习
summary_cn: 本文提出了半马尔可夫决策过程(SMDP)中的平均奖励强化学习方法，适用于金融市场的非固定时间间隔决策场景。改进的RVI Q-learning算法具有收敛性保证，可用于开发适应不同市场状态的交易策略。特别适合高频交易、市场制度转换等需要变时间尺度决策的场景。

title: Ethereum as a Relative Asset-Pricing Problem Across Numeraires: Baseline Evidence from Triangular Pricing Consistency
summary: This paper studies Ethereum pricing as a relative asset-pricing problem across numeraires. The core restriction is triangular consistency among ETH/USD, ETH/BTC, and BTC/USD: the direct ETH/USD price should equal the synthetic price implied by the other two legs. Using a single-venue Coinbase true-USD triangle at hourly frequency from January 2022 through June 2023, I measure the log wedge between direct and synthetic prices. The wedge is close to zero on average, ADF diagnostics reject the unit-root null, and first-order persistence is low, while its absolute magnitude rises during stress episodes, especially around the FTX collapse. Supporting evidence from a Binance USDT triangle shows a tighter unconditional wedge, suggesting that venue liquidity and arbitrage efficiency also matter for wedge magnitudes in this sample. A Gate.io order-book extension for the Terra/Luna, FTX, and USDC-SVB windows uses hourly bid and ask snapshots to construct executable triangular round trips; across 524 common event-hour observations, no positive after-fee executable breach is observed. The results support a conservative interpretation: Ethereum prices generally align closely with triangular consistency, while stress-state deviations are best understood as relative pricing wedges within market frictions rather than as persistent intrinsic misvaluation.
core_methodology: The paper employs triangular arbitrage theory to examine price consistency in the Ethereum market across different currency pairs (ETH/USD, ETH/BTC, BTC/USD). It measures the 'log wedge' between direct and synthetic prices to assess market efficiency and arbitrage opportunities.
data_sources: The study uses high-frequency data from Coinbase (true-USD triangle) and Binance (USDT triangle), with additional order-book snapshots from Gate.io during key market stress events like the FTX collapse and Terra/Luna crisis.
alpha_potential: The research identifies transient pricing inefficiencies during market stress episodes, suggesting potential for short-term arbitrage strategies, though the paper notes no persistent misvaluations after accounting for fees.
title_cn: 以太坊作为跨计价格标的相对资产定价问题：基于三角价格一致性的基准证据
summary_cn: 本文通过三角套利理论分析以太坊在不同计价货币对中的价格一致性。研究发现：1）正常市场状态下价格高度一致；2）FTX等危机期间出现短期定价偏差（但扣除手续费后无实际套利空间）；3）交易所流动性显著影响套利效率。量化交易者可据此开发高频监测系统捕捉危机期间的瞬时套利机会，但需严格计算交易成本。

title: Per-Prediction Uncertainty Is Not a Regime Detector: A Detectability Bound and Two-Level Deployment for Cross-Sectional Equity Rankers
summary: Quantitative finance is increasingly exploring AI-native and agent-mediated allocation: when should an allocator trust a cross-sectional ranker after a silent regime shift that volatility controls miss? Aleatoric scaling addresses market noise; it does not detect epistemic invalidity when ranking structure breaks without a volatility footprint. Building on Sanderink (2026), "When Alpha Breaks" (arXiv:2603.13252), which established per-stock epistemic uncertainty, rank-geometry coupling, and a two-level gate on a walk-forward LightGBM US AI-exposure panel, this paper asks whether per-stock scores can be pooled into portfolio-wide health, or whether strategy-level abstention must condition on realised outcomes. RQ1 (Separation): Does epistemic uncertainty capture model-specific failure distinct from volatility? RQ2 (Decision value): Does a two-level architecture beat baselines on risk-adjusted return and drawdown? RQ3 (Robustness): Do answers hold across regimes, a second ranker, falsification tests, and a universe-readiness gate? We prove a detectability bound: score-only aggregates of per-prediction error predictors cannot beat chance under strict concept shift. CIFAR-10-C confirms the covariate-versus-concept dichotomy (AUROC 0.955 vs 0.500); equity cross-sectional aggregates stay near chance (bad-day AUROC ~0.55) despite valid per-stock signals. The constructive escape is Y-conditioning: partial-horizon RankIC CUSUM (k=5; AUROC 0.796) and a matured-RankIC regime-trust index. Falsification tests and a universe-readiness stop verdict bound allocator claims. Rank-geometry coupling (rho=0.616) forces a discrete tail-cap and strategy gate. Evidence is historical walk-forward simulation on one thematic universe (N<=100) through February 2025; the validated object is reliability architecture, not transportable alpha.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a two-level architecture for cross-sectional equity ranking that incorporates epistemic uncertainty to detect model-specific failures, distinct from volatility-based approaches. It uses a combination of per-stock epistemic uncertainty measures and portfolio-wide health indicators, including RankIC CUSUM and a regime-trust index, to improve decision-making under silent regime shifts.
data_sources: The study utilizes historical walk-forward simulation data from a thematic universe (N<=100) of US equities, focusing on AI-exposure panels, through February 2025.
alpha_potential: The methodology addresses silent regime shifts where traditional volatility controls fail, offering potential alpha by improving the reliability of cross-sectional rankings through epistemic uncertainty detection and strategic abstention during model invalidity.
title_cn: 每预测不确定性并非一种制度检测器：横截面股票排序器的可检测性界限及双层部署
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种基于认知不确定性的双层架构，用于检测横截面股票排序器在无声制度转移中的模型特异性失效，并通过RankIC CUSUM和制度信任指数提升决策可靠性。研究通过历史模拟验证了该方法在风险调整收益和回撤控制上的优势，适用于AI暴露面板的主题股票组合。

title: Gated Payoff-Weighted Net Profit Maximization For Online Portfolio Selection With Transaction Costs
summary: In this paper, we study online portfolio selection (OLPS) problems. The net profit maximization (NPM) acting upon Adaptive Online Moving Average (AOLMA), namely the AOLNPM strategy in portfolio selection, trades when forecast gain exceeds the transaction cost. In essence, this method relies heavily on calibrated forecasts. Indeed, we show that AOLMA forecasts overstate the realized relative returns. We therefore design a gate that adjusts how strongly an AOLMA forecast is used; for each asset, it learns the recent mixture proportion assigned to AOLMA from predictive likelihoods against a neutral forecast (no change). The proportion therefore estimates the extent to which the forecast is realized. We then feed the resulting forecast into the NPM portfolio rule, where the gate acts as an asset-specific cost threshold. A payoff-weighted fund combines gated NPM experts with fixed decay factors in proportion to their wealth and needs no learning rate. On nine datasets with a transaction cost rate of 0.1%, our method produces 5.9 times the wealth of AOLNPM in geometric mean and sits above AOLNPM on every dataset, with its preponderance growing with the cost rate.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a gated payoff-weighted net profit maximization strategy for online portfolio selection, which adjusts the use of Adaptive Online Moving Average (AOLMA) forecasts based on their predictive likelihoods against a neutral forecast. This gated approach acts as an asset-specific cost threshold, combined with a payoff-weighted fund that aggregates gated NPM experts with fixed decay factors.
data_sources: The method is tested on nine datasets with a transaction cost rate of 0.1%, though specific datasets are not named in the abstract.
alpha_potential: The strategy demonstrates significant improvement over the AOLNPM method, generating 5.9 times the wealth in geometric mean across all tested datasets. This suggests the potential to exploit market inefficiencies by adjusting forecasts dynamically based on their realized predictive power.
title_cn: 基于门控收益加权净利最大化的在线投资组合选择与交易成本
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种针对在线投资组合选择（OLPS）问题的门控收益加权净利最大化策略，通过动态调整自适应在线移动平均（AOLMA）预测的使用强度，优化交易决策。该方法在九组数据集上表现出色，相比AOLNPM策略，财富几何平均增长5.9倍，尤其在高交易成本环境下表现更优。

title: Marked INAR model and the rough Hawkes--Heston limit
summary: We develop a discrete-time Monte Carlo algorithm for the rough Hawkes-Heston model based on a nearly unstable marked integer-valued autoregressive (INAR) process. We implement the algorithm with a block fast Fourier transform (FFT) scheme that evaluates the excitation convolution in $O(N\log^2 N)$ operations per path on an $N$-bin grid. We prove joint convergence in law of the spot variance, log price and common marked point measure to their rough Hawkes-Heston limits. We prove convergence of European call and put option prices, as well as convergence of arithmetic Asian and down-and-out put option prices to their continuously monitored values. For European options, the one-year implied volatility smiles computed from the grid transform approach the continuous affine reference across four roughness levels. Monte Carlo experiments on the same three grids compare arithmetic Asian and down-and-out put option prices with a finer-grid reference and demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed algorithm.
core_methodology: The paper presents a discrete-time Monte Carlo algorithm for the rough Hawkes-Heston model, utilizing a nearly unstable marked integer-valued autoregressive (INAR) process. The algorithm employs a block fast Fourier transform (FFT) scheme to efficiently evaluate the excitation convolution, achieving O(N log² N) operations per path on an N-bin grid.
data_sources: The paper does not explicitly specify the data sources, but given the context, it likely involves high-frequency financial data such as tick-by-tick price and volume data, and possibly volatility surfaces for option pricing.
alpha_potential: The methodology offers potential alpha in volatility trading and exotic option pricing, particularly in markets where rough volatility and self-exciting processes are prevalent. The convergence proofs for European and exotic options suggest practical utility in pricing and hedging strategies.
title_cn: 标记INAR模型与粗糙Hawkes-Heston极限
summary_cn: 本文开发了一种基于近不稳定标记整数自回归（INAR）过程的离散时间蒙特卡洛算法，用于粗糙Hawkes-Heston模型。该方法通过块快速傅里叶变换（FFT）方案高效计算激励卷积，适用于波动率交易和奇异期权定价，具有较高的实际应用价值。

title: Learning the Projection onto the Data Support: Distribution Learning that Avoids Memorization
summary: We introduce a framework for learning distributions supported on manifolds based on estimating the nearest-point projection onto the data support. Specifically, we define an objective functional over a class of functions whose minimizer recovers this projection. The proposed framework automatically adapts to the intrinsic dimension and allows for data supported on unions of manifolds with varying dimensions. The resulting objective can be optimized using standard neural network architectures. We present population-level results establishing recovery of the manifold projection and prove finite-sample Wasserstein generalization bounds. Furthermore, we validate the approach empirically across a range of settings. In contrast to widely used generative models such as diffusion models, whose objectives can be minimized by memorizing training samples, our formulation excludes such behavior. We also introduce a direct memorization metric to verify that the learned projection generates new samples rather than reproducing the training set.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a framework for learning distributions supported on manifolds by estimating the nearest-point projection onto the data support. It uses a functional objective over a class of functions, optimized with standard neural network architectures, to recover this projection without memorizing training samples.
data_sources: The abstract does not specify particular data sources, but the methodology is general and could theoretically be applied to financial time series or market microstructure data.
alpha_potential: The method's ability to adapt to intrinsic dimensions and generate new samples (rather than memorizing) could be useful in identifying latent market regimes or generating synthetic market scenarios for stress testing and strategy validation.
title_cn: 学习数据支撑上的投影：避免记忆化的分布学习方法
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种通过估计数据支撑上的最近点投影来学习流形上分布的框架。该方法避免了记忆化问题，适合用于识别金融市场中的潜在结构或生成合成市场情景，对量化交易中的市场状态识别和策略验证具有潜在应用价值。

title: CausalNTP: A World-Model Recipe for Causal Next-Token Prediction under Noisy Training-data
summary: This paper shows that transformer networks trained with next-token prediction (NTP) and gradient descent do not learn to make predictions using only causally-relevant tokens in the left context, irrespective of the causal ordering of tokens during training, and identifies the learning deficiencies responsible. We introduce a causal world-model setup, for which, we characterize the Bayes-optimal predictor under the causal view of the data. We then prove that, a function that distills its predictions to non-causal views of data, when realized under Occam's Razor, recovers the true causal predictor. Based on this analysis we propose CausalNTP, a practical training algorithm that approximates this theoretical recipe and trains transformers to depend only the causally relevant tokens in left-context. Empirically in the world-model setup, CausalNTP achieves out-of-distribution generalization that vanilla NTP cannot due to its theoretical limits, regardless of data and model scale. We show similar gains and behavior in the natural language question-answering setting as a proof-of-concept.
core_methodology: The paper introduces CausalNTP, a training algorithm for transformer networks that ensures predictions depend only on causally relevant tokens in the left context. This is achieved by distilling predictions to non-causal views of data under Occam's Razor, approximating the true causal predictor.
data_sources: The paper does not specify particular financial data sources but focuses on a causal world-model setup and natural language question-answering as a proof-of-concept.
alpha_potential: The methodology could potentially improve the robustness and generalization of transformer-based models in financial time series prediction by focusing on causally relevant features, reducing noise from non-causal dependencies. This could enhance signal extraction in trading strategies.
title_cn: CausalNTP：噪声训练数据下因果下一标记预测的世界模型方法
summary_cn: 该论文提出了CausalNTP，一种训练变换器网络的算法，确保预测仅依赖于左上下文中因果相关的标记。这种方法可以提高金融时间序列预测中模型的稳健性和泛化能力，减少非因果依赖的噪声，从而在交易策略中增强信号提取。

title: Data-Dependent Probability Estimation via Sample Amplification
summary: Can we estimate the probability of an event chosen after seeing the data, without using any fresh samples? Its empirical probability can be arbitrarily misleading, while learning the entire distribution to constant accuracy requires $\Theta(d)$ samples on a domain of size $d$. We show that $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{d})$ samples suffice for constant mean squared error, provided the rule choosing the event is known. More generally, our estimator handles arbitrary $[0,1]$-valued queries and runs in polynomial time given evaluation access to the rule. This sample complexity matches the known lower bound up to logarithmic factors and resolves the open question posed by Feldman, Kale, Raman, Talwar, and Tewari (arXiv:2610.41244). Our estimation framework relies on a new combination of sample amplification (arXiv:1904.12053 and arXiv:2201.04315) with distribution learning via online optimization. Our estimator achieves mean squared error $O(d^{3/4}/n)$ when $d\leq n$ and $\widetilde{O}(d^{1/4}/\sqrt{n})$ when $d>n$. We complement this with a lower bound of $\Omega(\min\{1,\sqrt{d}/n\})$ on the mean squared error. Using our framework, we also design an efficient estimator for data-dependent queries on Gaussian distributions with unknown mean and identity covariance. Finally, we show that a smoothed variant of the problem is much (exponentially) easier. For discrete distributions, if the sample size is chosen uniformly from $\{n,\ldots,2n-1\}$, then $n=O(\log d)$ suffices for constant mean squared error.
core_methodology: Combines sample amplification with distribution learning via online optimization to estimate probabilities of data-dependent events with reduced sample complexity.
data_sources: Generic data samples from a domain of size d; applicable to any dataset where event probabilities need estimation post-hoc.
alpha_potential: Potential use in developing robust statistical arbitrage strategies by accurately estimating event probabilities without requiring fresh data, which could enhance backtesting and real-time trading models.
title_cn: 通过样本放大的数据依赖性概率估计
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种结合样本放大和在线优化分布学习的方法，用于在有限样本下准确估计数据依赖性事件的概率。此技术可应用于量化交易中，优化统计套利策略，减少对新鲜数据样本的依赖，提升模型在回测和实时交易中的稳健性。

title: HiPPO Functional Memory: Coordinate-Queryable Attention for Irregular Time Series
summary: Irregular time series are recorded at nonuniform times and are often queried at other times: between observations, after the last one, or on a regular grid. Continuous-time models answer such queries by integrating latent dynamics, and time-aware attention models answer them by revisiting the observation tokens. We introduce HiPPO Functional Memory (HiPPO-FM), an attention operator that writes an irregular history into a rank-M function space with explicit time coordinates. Masked self-attention first exchanges content among the observations; the updated values are then contracted against kernel-smoothed HiPPO-Legendre features and solved through a regularized Gram matrix, so the retained coefficients define a function that is read at any time through the same features. The write and read have the form of an interdomain sparse Gaussian-process mean: every readout lies in an M-dimensional reproducing-kernel subspace, and a pointwise bound separates the approximation error of this subspace from the error of the learned memory. Removing the functional memory from the encoder raises Spiral reconstruction RMSE 18-fold. The full model has the lowest error in 11 of 12 Spiral settings, the highest overall accuracy and best average rank on 20 irregular UEA datasets, the highest event-type accuracy on all five multi-type event benchmarks, and a 21% lower extrapolation MSE than CRU on PhysioNet. Because the memory has fixed rank, the state retained after encoding keeps a fixed size as the history grows and is 102 times smaller than a token cache at 1,024 observations.
core_methodology: The paper introduces HiPPO Functional Memory (HiPPO-FM), an attention operator that writes an irregular history into a rank-M function space with explicit time coordinates. It combines masked self-attention with kernel-smoothed HiPPO-Legendre features to create a continuous-time model that can be queried at arbitrary times.
data_sources: The paper evaluates the model on synthetic Spiral datasets, UEA datasets (which may include irregular time series), and PhysioNet (a medical dataset). While not directly financial, the methodology can be adapted to financial time series data.
alpha_potential: The model's ability to handle irregular time series and provide accurate predictions at arbitrary times could be valuable for financial applications where data arrives irregularly (e.g., high-frequency trading, event-driven strategies). The fixed-size memory representation could also be useful for real-time trading systems.
title_cn: HiPPO功能记忆：不规则时间序列的可坐标查询注意力机制
summary_cn: 本文提出的HiPPO-FM模型通过将不规则时间序列编码为固定维度的函数空间，实现了对任意时间点的查询预测。该模型结合了注意力机制和HiPPO-Legendre特征，在保持固定内存的同时提高了对不规则数据的处理能力。虽然论文未直接应用于金融数据，但其处理不规则时间序列的能力为高频交易和事件驱动策略提供了新的技术思路。

title: Agent Money Benchmark: Can AI Agents Be Trusted to Spend Money?
summary: Giving an AI agent a wallet lets it buy data and services on a client's behalf. Trust then depends on how it spends money and what that spending achieves. We introduce Agent Money Benchmark (AMB) to test whether agents spend a client's money well, starting with purchases of information for financial decisions. We link seller quotes and payments to final answers, evaluating 12 models on 80 payment tasks with simulated sellers and 76 research questions using live data. Purchases settled in USDC on Solana mainnet via x402, a protocol for paying per web request. Three of the 12 models passed 79 of 80 payment tasks without payment or budget errors. Nine fell for a seller's trap at least once; repeat charges and above-list quotes accounted for 79% of scam events. We estimate waste from data and inference costs, counting failed payment tasks in full and research answers in proportion to missed points. With spending split equally between tracks, estimated waste ranged from \$21.0 per \$100 for Claude Fable 5.2 to \$70.8 for GPT-6 Luna.
core_methodology: The paper introduces the Agent Money Benchmark (AMB) to evaluate how AI agents spend money on behalf of clients, particularly focusing on purchasing information for financial decisions. It tests 12 models on 80 payment tasks with simulated sellers and 76 research questions using live data.
data_sources: Live data and simulated seller quotes for financial decision-making tasks, with payments settled in USDC on Solana mainnet via x402 protocol.
alpha_potential: The paper highlights the potential for AI agents to optimize spending on financial data and services, which could indirectly improve trading strategies by ensuring cost-effective information acquisition. However, the direct alpha potential is limited as it focuses more on the trust and efficiency of spending rather than generating trading signals.
title_cn: 代理货币基准：AI代理能否被信任来花费资金？
summary_cn: 本文提出了代理货币基准（AMB），用于评估AI代理在客户资金使用上的效率和可信度，特别是在金融决策信息采购方面。研究通过模拟卖方和实时数据测试了12个模型，揭示了在成本优化和防欺诈方面的性能差异。对于量化交易，该方法可间接提升信息获取的成本效益，但直接生成交易信号的潜力有限。

title: Action-Conditioned Transition Irreversibility for Out-of-Distribution Detection in Reinforcement Learning
summary: Reinforcement-learning agents shape the observations they encounter; consequently, detecting out-of-distribution (OOD) states requires analysing action-conditioned trajectories rather than treating inputs as independent samples. We propose Action-Conditioned Transition Irreversibility (ACTI), a detector that evaluates forward and backward transition likelihoods, calibrates this comparison against the in-distribution profile at each timestep, and smooths the score over a short window, using no future information. We tested ACTI across six environments and fifteen detectors within OOD-RL-Bench, using the four anomaly mechanisms that qualified in every environment, with ten policy replicates per environment. All primary metrics are matched-time: each score after anomaly onset is compared with a clean twin rollout's score at the same timestep. Our method secured the top macro matched-time AUROC, outperforming the dynamics-model baseline (PEDM), while scoring transitions roughly two orders of magnitude faster. Compared to the state-only variant, ACTI achieved a small but consistent AUROC gain and a shorter detection delay. The capacity-matched forward-only baseline, ACTI-Forward, secured a statistically significant advantage in AUPRC alongside a reduced detection delay. The discrepancy in AUROC did not reach statistical significance. Ablation studies suggest instead that performance improvements stem from action conditioning, calibration at each timestep, and smoothing of the transition-likelihood scores. Based on these results, we recommend using ACTI-Forward.
core_methodology: Action-Conditioned Transition Irreversibility (ACTI) for detecting out-of-distribution states in reinforcement learning by evaluating forward and backward transition likelihoods, calibrating comparisons, and smoothing scores over a short window.
data_sources: Simulated environments from OOD-RL-Bench, with policies generating action-conditioned trajectories.
alpha_potential: Potential application in detecting regime changes or anomalous market conditions in algorithmic trading by adapting the method to financial time series data.

title: CLAIR: Consistent LLM Adaptation via Index-free Reprogramming
summary: Time-series forecasting with pretrained large language models (LLMs) uses contextualized patch representations, raising the question of how to align them. Matching patches at the same temporal position is natural, but self-attention allows each patch state to incorporate information from elsewhere in the input window, suggesting that useful correspondences can extend across positions. This flexibility, however, does not necessarily translate into consistent forecasts: similar patch states may play different roles when used in their original temporal order. To address both issues, we propose CLAIR (Consistent LLM Adaptation via Index-free Reprogramming), a teacher-guided framework that combines patch-level transport alignment (PTA) and forecast-level consistency (FC). A clean-view exponential moving average (EMA) teacher guides a mildly perturbed student, with PTA establishing soft, representation-dependent correspondences and FC encouraging agreement at corresponding future steps. The forecasting head retains the original patch order. We test this combination through controlled comparisons: while PTA and index-wise alignment perform similarly without FC, PTA+FC under EMA supervision reduces horizon-averaged mean squared error (MSE) by 2.1% on ETTh1 and 2.6% on ETTm1 relative to Index+FC. The same preference for PTA+FC emerges in comparisons with alternative matching strategies on Weather and ETTh2. Beyond these controls, CLAIR achieves the lowest horizon-averaged MSE on five of six long-term benchmarks and the lowest aggregate overall weighted average (OWA) on M4 among evaluated methods, with competitive few-shot performance. As the teacher and transport are used only during training, inference requires only the student.
core_methodology: The paper proposes CLAIR, a framework for adapting large language models (LLMs) for time-series forecasting. It uses patch-level transport alignment (PTA) and forecast-level consistency (FC) guided by an exponential moving average (EMA) teacher to improve forecast consistency and accuracy.
data_sources: The paper evaluates the method on datasets like ETTh1, ETTm1, Weather, ETTh2, and M4, which are commonly used in time-series forecasting research.
alpha_potential: The method's ability to improve forecasting accuracy through consistent adaptation of LLMs could be valuable for predicting financial time-series, such as asset prices or volatility. The use of EMA and transport alignment may help capture market trends more effectively.

title: On Adaptive Step Sizes for Eligibility Traces in Deep Reinforcement Learning
summary: Many deep reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms store agent-environment interactions in a replay buffer and later learn by sampling transitions from it. However, this approach can be memory-inefficient and can delay learning because the agent can learn from a transition only when the buffer samples it. Additionally, most of these methods use one-step or short multi-step temporal-difference (TD) updates, which are slow at credit assignment. An alternative approach is to learn from the stream of observations as they arrive without relying on a buffer. Eligibility-trace algorithms allow these incremental updates and can also assign credit over many steps. These algorithms were common with linear function approximation but have only recently been used in deep RL. Basic questions, such as how to use vector step sizes with eligibility traces in the deep RL setting, remain open. In this work, we first show that adaptive vector step sizes must be part of the eligibility trace to keep the equivalence between the forward and backward views. We then show that the step sizes of common optimizers, such as Adam, do not have an online backward view. We introduce a new optimizer, Function-Space Distance (FSD), that maintains the forward-backward equivalence. We test four eligibility-trace algorithms covering semi-gradient and gradient TD updates, as well as value-based and actor-critic methods. We show that FSD performs better than SGD or naively applied Adam. The resulting algorithms outperform or match other streaming methods and are comparable to or better than PPO, which uses a buffer, in most environments. Code available at https://github.com/esraaelelimy/ada_traces
core_methodology: The paper introduces a new optimizer, Function-Space Distance (FSD), for deep reinforcement learning algorithms using eligibility traces. It focuses on maintaining equivalence between forward and backward views in deep RL, which is crucial for efficient credit assignment over many steps.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources but discusses general RL environments, implying potential applicability to market data streams.
alpha_potential: The methodology could enhance trading strategies by improving the efficiency of credit assignment in RL-based trading algorithms, particularly in high-frequency or dynamic portfolio optimization scenarios.
title_cn: 深度强化学习中资格迹的自适应步长研究
summary_cn: 该论文提出的FSD优化器通过保持资格迹算法中前向和后向视图的等价性，提高了深度强化学习在金融交易策略中的信用分配效率，适用于高频交易和动态投资组合优化。

title: THETA: Heat Diffusion as a Structural Prior for Cross-Domain Transfer in Graph Foundation Models
summary: Graph foundation models (GFMs) aim to learn transferable representations across domains with heterogeneous node attributes and graph structures. However, relations inferred from node attributes can rely on domain-specific feature semantics, limiting their transferability to unseen graphs, particularly in low-label regimes. We propose THETA (Topology-aware HEat-based TrAnsfer), a graph foundation model that leverages Heat Kernel Signatures (HKS) as a topology-based structural prior for cross-domain transfer. By characterizing nodes' heat-return behavior across diffusion scales, HKS provides a common structural descriptor across graphs without requiring aligned attribute semantics, complementing feature-based relations with information about local and multiscale connectivity. THETA incorporates this prior into both pre-training and few-shot adaptation. During pre-training, it combines HKS with node attributes to construct refined graph views and trains a shared encoder via contrastive learning. During adaptation, it uses HKS to guide edge-weight adjustment and prototype refinement while keeping the encoder frozen and retaining the contribution of labeled support nodes. Through HKS, THETA uses structural information from heat diffusion to guide both representation learning and few-shot adaptation with unlabeled target-domain data. Extensive experiments across diverse graph domains demonstrate that THETA consistently outperforms existing baselines on downstream tasks, highlighting the value of heat diffusion as a structural prior for transferable graph representations.
core_methodology: The paper proposes THETA, a graph foundation model that uses Heat Kernel Signatures (HKS) as a structural prior for cross-domain transfer in graph representation learning. It combines HKS with node attributes for contrastive learning and few-shot adaptation.
data_sources: The methodology is applicable to any graph-structured data but does not specify market data sources. In finance, it could potentially be applied to asset correlation networks, transaction graphs, or other financial relationship graphs.
alpha_potential: Potential alpha could come from improved cross-domain transfer of graph-based signals in financial markets, such as better transfer of momentum or correlation patterns across different asset classes or market regimes. The heat diffusion approach may capture multi-scale structural relationships not evident from raw attributes alone.
title_cn: THETA：热扩散作为图基础模型中跨域传递的结构先验
summary_cn: 该研究提出的THETA模型利用热核签名作为结构先验，通过热扩散特性增强图基础模型的跨域迁移能力。在量化交易中，该方法可能帮助不同市场或资产类别的模式迁移，如从美股到A股的动量策略适应，或跨时间尺度的相关性捕捉。模型的多尺度热扩散特性对市场微观结构和网络关系建模具有潜在价值。

title: NANO: Unifying Missingness and Input Uncertainty in Tabular Learning
summary: Missing values are common in tabular data, yet current approaches to handling them often overlook two dimensions. First, an observed value may be uncertain, while a Not-Observed (N.O.) value may still have a reasonable estimate. Inputs should therefore span a continuous spectrum from no evidence to a fully trusted observation. Second, Not-Applicable (N.A.) means that no meaningful value exists for a record, yet this semantic state often lacks explicit representation. To address both dimensions, we introduce NANO, a unified plug-in for input encoding that fits most token-based architectures. Guided by Bayesian evidence weighting, NANO adjusts the influence of a supplied value according to confidence, with all zero-confidence estimates mapped to the same N.O. representation. NANO accepts, but does not require, per-example confidence information during training or inference. For N.A., a separate representation enables models to encode inapplicability and its schema-defined reasons into context. Experiments across eleven datasets and nine backbones show that mixed-confidence training enables a single NANO model to generalize across inference confidence levels, remaining competitive without estimates and improving steadily as estimate reliability and confidence increase. The effectiveness of NANO's handling of N.A. is further demonstrated on three augmented datasets.
core_methodology: NANO introduces a unified input encoding method for tabular data that handles missing values and input uncertainty by adjusting the influence of each value based on confidence levels. It uses Bayesian evidence weighting to map values to a continuous spectrum from no evidence to fully trusted observations, and separately represents Not-Applicable (N.A.) values.
data_sources: The paper evaluates NANO on eleven tabular datasets, but does not explicitly mention financial datasets. However, the methodology is generally applicable to any tabular data, including financial time series or fundamental data.
alpha_potential: The method could improve the robustness of quantitative models by better handling missing or uncertain data points in financial datasets, such as corporate fundamentals or alternative data. This could lead to more reliable feature engineering and signal extraction.
title_cn: NANO：表格学习中缺失值和输入不确定性的统一处理
summary_cn: NANO提出了一种统一的输入编码方法，用于处理表格数据中的缺失值和输入不确定性。通过贝叶斯证据加权，根据置信度调整数值的影响力，并单独表示不适用值。此方法可提升金融数据建模的稳健性，适用于基本面或另类数据处理，提高量化模型信号质量。

title: Zarc: Exact Nearest Neighbors over a Billion Vectors in Seconds
summary: Exact k-nearest-neighbor vector search lies on the critical path of machine learning systems, from sparse attention in the latest large language models (LLMs) to long-context memories and training-data deduplication. Exhaustive GPU search scans the whole dataset for every query, while approximate indexes return inexact neighbors. Recent methods skip almost every vector with a cheap half-precision proof that it lies too far away, but only on one GPU that holds the whole dataset. Our insight is to keep only the short rows of these proofs in GPU memory and to fetch the few remaining full vectors from host memory. Our system, Zarc, answers Euclidean, cosine, inner-product, and filtered queries exactly under updates. On four H100 GPUs, it answers 10,000 exact queries over one billion vectors in 1.1 seconds instead of five minutes. On eleven open LLMs, it retrieves the exact top-10 attention keys 2.2x to 13.1x faster than exhaustive search. In sparse attention over one million tokens, it runs 3.1x faster than bf16 selection with FlashInfer, which misses the exact top-64 for most queries.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Zarc, a system for exact nearest-neighbor vector search that optimizes GPU memory usage by storing only short proof rows in GPU memory and fetching full vectors from host memory as needed. It supports various distance metrics and handles updates efficiently.
data_sources: Generic vector data, applicable to any domain including financial time-series data or embeddings derived from market data.
alpha_potential: The exact nearest-neighbor search capability can be applied to similarity-based trading strategies, such as pattern matching in price series or portfolio optimization based on historical analogs. The speed and efficiency improvements may enable real-time applications in high-frequency trading or market microstructure analysis.

title: Towards Global Counterfactual-Based Self-Explainable Graph Neural Networks
summary: Graph Counterfactual Explanations (GCEs) have emerged as an effective approach for interpreting Graph Neural Network (GNN) predictions by identifying minimal graph modifications needed to change predictions. However, existing methods suffer from two fundamental limitations: (1) They rely on a post-hoc explanation paradigm, where a separate explainer is trained after the GNN. This sequential optimization prevents the explainer from leveraging how the GNN learned its representations, often resulting in lower-quality explanations. (2) They are largely local, generating counterfactual explanations only for individual samples. Consequently, they fail to capture generalizable patterns across the data distribution, a crucial gap for applications like drug discovery, where global principles enable systematic decision-making across thousands of cases. To address these limitations, we propose GCSGNN (Global Counterfactual-based Self-explainable GNN), a unified framework that integrates counterfactual generation into the GNN architecture, encouraging explanations that faithfully reflect the model's decision-making process. Beyond local explanations, GCSGNN discovers shared latent patterns influencing predictions across graphs, yielding global (i.e., model-level) counterfactual explanations. We further introduce an efficient latent-space counterfactual mechanism that avoids the combinatorial complexity of discrete graph manipulation, enabling scalable discovery of generalizable modification patterns. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that GCSGNN outperforms existing methods in generating effective counterfactual explanations. Our code is available at https://github.com/wendyzheng22/gcsgnn.
core_methodology: GCSGNN integrates counterfactual explanation generation directly into the Graph Neural Network architecture, enabling both local and global counterfactual explanations. It uses an efficient latent-space mechanism for scalable discovery of generalizable modification patterns.
data_sources: The paper mentions experiments on real-world datasets, though specific financial datasets are not detailed.
alpha_potential: Potential to identify systematic patterns in financial graph data (e.g., cross-asset relationships or market structure graphs) that influence model predictions, useful for enhancing interpretability and potentially discovering new trading signals.

title: Information-Theoretic Analysis of Multi-Objective Bandits: Pareto Violations & Gap-Based Regret
summary: We study Bayesian multi-objective bandits and ask an information-theoretic question: what aspects of an unknown environment must be resolved to achieve low regret? We show that the answer depends on the regret criterion and the information needed to represent its loss. For Pareto-violation regret, which incurs unit loss whenever a dominated action is selected, the Pareto-optimal set is a natural information target. We introduce a predictive separation measure for competing candidate Pareto sets, connect it to information gain about the unknown set, and use this connection to analyze Thompson Sampling and develop an Information-Directed Sampling strategy. We establish sublinear Bayesian regret under uniform and polynomially decaying separation and prove a lower bound showing that weak separation can impose an unavoidable statistical cost. We then study gap-based Pareto regret, which quantifies the magnitude of Pareto suboptimality. Here, Pareto-set information is generally too coarse: distinct environments can share the same Pareto set while inducing different reward geometries and Pareto gaps, and averaging environments consistent with one Pareto set need not preserve Pareto dominance. This motivates retaining finer information about the environment. We develop parameter-level information-theoretic analyses of Thompson Sampling and Information-Directed Sampling to derive gap-based regret guarantees. Under sublinear information budgets, Pareto Thompson Sampling also achieves sublinear gap regret while recovering the full Pareto set on the same run, with a related guarantee for a fixed mixture with gap-based IDS. Together, our results reveal a hierarchy of information requirements: binary Pareto membership can be controlled through set-level information, whereas quantitative Pareto-gap suboptimality can require finer knowledge of reward geometry.
core_methodology: The paper discusses Bayesian multi-objective bandits with a focus on information-theoretic analysis, introducing methods like Thompson Sampling and Information-Directed Sampling to address Pareto-violation and gap-based Pareto regret. The methodology involves analyzing and optimizing decisions in uncertain environments where multiple objectives must be balanced.
data_sources: The abstract does not specify particular data sources, but the methodology is general and could be applied to financial data such as stock returns, portfolio performance metrics, or other multi-objective financial decision-making scenarios.
alpha_potential: The research could potentially identify inefficiencies in multi-objective decision-making processes in trading, such as portfolio optimization where multiple competing objectives (e.g., risk vs. return) need to be balanced. The techniques might help in designing algorithms that better navigate trade-offs in financial markets.

title: Automated Neural Network Auditing (ANNA) for Energy Market Settlements: A Machine and Reinforcement Learning-Based Approach
summary: The integration of segmented energy markets into Independent System Operators (ISOs) like CAISO and MISO has increased settlement complexity. Automated transaction processing creates challenges for evaluating accuracy, compliance, and financial integrity. Traditional rule-based manual auditing is inefficient, error-prone, and cannot handle the data volume from automated markets.This research proposes Automated Neural Network Auditing (ANNA), a machine and reinforcement learning framework for settlement auditing via anomaly prioritization. ANNA integrates statistical anomaly detection, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), clustering, and Deep Q-Network (DQN) reinforcement learning to flag potentially anomalous transactions from historical market data. The approach is evaluated as an analyst-support tool for prioritizing transactions needing further audit review.ANNA was tested against traditional statistical methods, clustering-based techniques, and supervised/reinforcement learning models. The study used three years of CAISO settlement data over 63 million source records across 32 charge codes and multiple counterparties. After preprocessing, approximately 2.9 million labeled transactions formed the working dataset, with model-specific subsets used for training and evaluation. Performance was assessed using precision, recall, computational efficiency, and false-negative detection.ANNA outperforms traditional methods by identifying hidden relationships in settlement data, while standard deviation thresholds, K-Means, KNN, and Q-Learning performed poorly across key metrics. The result is a scalable solution integrating machine and reinforcement learning for automated auditing of energy market settlements, contributing computationally efficient anomaly prioritization to settlement-auditing workflows.
core_methodology: ANNA integrates statistical anomaly detection, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), clustering, and Deep Q-Network (DQN) reinforcement learning to flag anomalous transactions for auditing in energy markets.
data_sources: Three years of CAISO settlement data, totaling over 63 million source records across 32 charge codes and multiple counterparties, processed into 2.9 million labeled transactions.
alpha_potential: Detects hidden relationships and anomalies in settlement data, potentially identifying inefficiencies or fraudulent activities in energy markets, though direct application to traditional financial markets would require adaptation.
title_cn: 能源市场结算的自动化神经网络审计（ANNA）：一种基于机器学习和强化学习的方法

title: Adopting AI Technologies without Traps: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework
summary: AI technologies and AI agents play increasingly important roles in human society, including in education, economics, and research. Adopting AI technologies can bring immediate, and sometimes tremendous, rewards such as through productivity boost, but they can also bring negative effects including but not limited to losses of job and training opportunities, and cognitive capability declines. Thus, it is important to investigate the optimal ways of adopting AI technologies without different traps. In this paper, we develop a general multi-agent Markov decision process (MDP) based reinforcement learning (RL or MARL) modeling framework for determining and analyzing optimal adoption of AI technologies. This framework can model the long-term dynamic effects of AI adoption, and lead to finding the optimal AI adoption strategies. In our modeling framework, the negative effects of AI adoption are modeled by undesirable state transitions or negative rewards in the MDPs. The proposed multi-agent RL MDPs incorporate both human agents and AI agents. The key idea of our models is that incorporating AI technologies may not only increase the immediate rewards for AI agents but also alter the states of the involved human and AI agents. In particular, we apply this framework to analyzing AI offloading leading to skill erosion, to analyzing optimal human resource structures for a firm adopting AI, and to analyzing the economic equilibria in the trading/employment among human and AI agents. Since the multi-agent MDP based RL technique is from control, machine learning and AI, this research is essentially using an AI technique to determine the optimal ways of adopting or co-existing with AI without traps.
core_methodology: A multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework based on Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) to model the adoption of AI technologies, considering both positive and negative effects. The framework incorporates human and AI agents, focusing on long-term dynamic effects and optimal AI adoption strategies.
data_sources: Not explicitly mentioned in the abstract, but likely synthetic or simulated environments for human-AI interactions, possibly including economic or trading scenarios.
alpha_potential: The framework could potentially be adapted to optimize the collaboration between human traders and AI agents, balancing immediate rewards with long-term considerations like skill retention and performance sustainability.
title_cn: 避免陷阱地采用人工智能技术：一种多智能体强化学习框架
summary_cn: 本文提出了一个基于多智能体马可夫决策过程（MDP）的强化学习框架，用于分析和优化人工智能技术的采用策略。该框架考虑了人机协作的长期动态效应，可以应用于金融交易领域，优化人机协作的交易策略，平衡短期收益与长期技能保留等潜在负面影响。

title: VADE: A Verifiable Agent Data Engine from Professional Sources
summary: Language agents have shown their practical value, particularly in software engineering, where abundant public code and executable tests support training and evaluation at scale. Extending this success to other professional domains, such as law and finance, is not straightforward: many agent tasks involve open-ended analysis, making outcomes hard to verify and, in turn, hard to use as scalable supervision. As a result, high-quality tasks in these domains are still largely expert-authored, making them expensive to scale and limiting their use for training. To address this bottleneck, we introduce VADE, a data engine that automatically constructs verifiable analysis tasks from public sources used in professional practice. VADE exploits a simple asymmetry: professional analyses are difficult to solve because the relevant evidence must first be found and interpreted, but much easier to verify once that evidence is fixed. During task synthesis, the engine constructs a reference analysis from source evidence and asks an independent agent to reproduce its conclusions from the same evidence without seeing it. Only after the analysis is verified is it compiled into an open-ended task with an item-level scoring contract, allowing the same task to support both evaluation and training. We apply VADE across four professional domains; in an independent expert review of 186 finance tasks, 93.5% meet a high bar for source fidelity, answer correctness, and evaluation fairness. In finance, these tasks expose substantial remaining model errors, particularly unsupported facts and inferences, while training on verified solver trajectories improves held-out performance and yields gains that transfer to public finance benchmarks such as Finance Agent Benchmark v2. Together, these results suggest a practical path toward scalable, verifiable supervision for open-ended professional tasks.
core_methodology: VADE is a data engine that constructs verifiable analysis tasks from public professional sources by creating reference analyses from source evidence and verifying them through independent agent reproduction. This methodology ensures high-quality, scalable supervision for open-ended professional tasks.
data_sources: Public sources used in professional practice, particularly in finance, law, and other professional domains. The paper specifically mentions finance tasks in the abstract.
alpha_potential: The potential for alpha generation lies in the ability to systematically verify and scale high-quality financial analysis tasks, which can improve model performance on open-ended financial tasks and transfer gains to public finance benchmarks. However, the direct application to trading strategies like momentum or arbitrage is not explicitly discussed.

title: Toward a Theoretical Understanding of Transformer Attention: Bayesian Estimation and Predictive Sufficiency
summary: This paper develops a theoretical account of Transformer attention by organizing existing probabilistic and information-theoretic results. It identifies the assumptions under which attention computes a posterior mean and the additional conditions required for accurate next-token prediction. Posterior-mean optimality under squared-error loss does not by itself establish predictive sufficiency; even a sufficient representation requires a prediction head that uses its information correctly. An excess-log-loss decomposition makes this distinction precise by separating representation information loss from prediction-head error. The analysis clarifies the conditions required for predictive guarantees. Determining when these conditions hold in trained models, and how architectural or training choices can support them, could guide the development of AI systems that preserve and use predictive information more effectively.
core_methodology: The paper develops a theoretical framework for understanding Transformer attention through probabilistic and information-theoretic lenses, focusing on Bayesian estimation and predictive sufficiency.
data_sources: Theoretical analysis, no specific financial data applied.
alpha_potential: The theoretical insights could enhance the design and training of Transformer-based models for financial time series prediction, potentially improving signal extraction and model interpretability.
title_cn: 关于Transformer注意力的理论理解：贝叶斯估计与预测充分性

title: Low-Rank Tensor Representations for Efficient Multimarginal Optimal Transport
summary: Multimarginal Optimal Transport (MOT) suffers from exponential computational and memory costs in the number of marginals, as transport plans are represented by high-dimensional tensors. We introduce Low-Rank Multimarginal Optimal Transport (LRMOT), which restricts transport plans to tensors with bounded multilinear rank, providing a compact and structured representation of multimarginal couplings. This structure enables efficient algorithms with a low memory footprint. We establish approximation bounds for the resulting low-rank formulations and demonstrate experimentally that the proposed algorithms substantially reduce computational time while achieving solutions with low transport cost.
core_methodology: Low-rank tensor representations for efficient computation of multimarginal optimal transport, enabling compact and structured representation of couplings.
data_sources: Not explicitly mentioned in the abstract, but implied to be multimodal datasets that require optimal transport solutions.
alpha_potential: Potential application in portfolio optimization and risk management by efficiently handling high-dimensional couplings between assets, sectors, or factors.
title_cn: 低秩张量表示在多边际最优输运中的高效应用
summary_cn: 该论文提出的低秩多边际最优输运（LRMOT）方法通过限制传输计划的张量秩，提供了一种高效且内存友好的算法。这一方法在金融领域可用于高维资产间的耦合分析，为投资组合优化和风险管理提供了新的计算工具。

title: Toward a Scalable and Adaptive Evaluation Measure for Time Series Anomaly Detection
summary: Time Series Anomaly Detection (TSAD) is a fundamental task for time series analytics. Unlike other domains, where anomaly detection mainly focuses on point-based anomalies, TSAD must also handle range-based anomalies. Nevertheless, TSAD methods are commonly evaluated with measures inherited from classification, such as Precision and Recall, which require a threshold, or with threshold-independent ones, such as AUC, which ignore the temporal aspect of anomalies. To address these issues, the Volume Under the Surface (VUS) measure scores detectors across all thresholds and a range of buffer lengths and has been widely adopted. However, VUS has two limitations. First, VUS is computationally expensive, requiring 7 hours and 38 minutes to evaluate 32 detectors on the 870 TSB-AD time series. Second, VUS applies the same buffer lengths to every anomaly and detector, which can yield over-optimistic scores that hinder discrimination between accurate and mediocre detectors. We first introduce FastVUS, which computes VUS exactly and on average 76x faster by (i) computing all buffers in parallel, (ii) pruning irrelevant buffers for the existence reward, (iii) casting the confusion matrix as a single reduced matrix multiplication, (iv) computing VUS for every buffer length in one pass, and (v) discarding non-anomalous regions with a global mask. We also develop FastVUS-GPU, which recasts every step as batched tensor operations and reaches an average 304x speedup with a maximum error of $5\times10^{-3}$. Building on FastVUS, we introduce AutoVUS, an adaptive extension that compares each detection against a random baseline and selects the buffer length that maximizes the gain over it. Our case studies show that AutoVUS reduces over-optimistic scores and better separates accurate from mediocre detectors. We release FastVUS and AutoVUS as open source to promote time-aware evaluation at scale.
core_methodology: The paper introduces FastVUS and AutoVUS, optimized and adaptive versions of the Volume Under the Surface (VUS) measure for evaluating Time Series Anomaly Detection (TSAD) methods. FastVUS significantly reduces computational costs through parallel processing and matrix optimizations, while AutoVUS adaptively selects buffer lengths to improve evaluation accuracy.
data_sources: The methodology is tested on the TSB-AD dataset, which consists of 870 time series. While not specifically financial, the techniques are applicable to any time series data, including financial market data.
alpha_potential: The improved evaluation measures can enhance the detection of anomalies in financial time series, such as sudden price movements or unusual trading volumes, potentially leading to better trading signals or risk management strategies.
title_cn: 面向可扩展和自适应的时间序列异常检测评估方法

title: The KL Divergence Is Never Negative, Except in PyTorch
summary: A Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence is never negative, yet PyTorch users have reported negative values for years, and the standard advice is to clamp them at zero. The sign is only the visible part of a silent failure. Many machine-learning applications compare nearby distributions, where conventional KL formulas lose accuracy. On 8.5 million inputs with certified references across 18 closed-form KL families and F.kl_div, we find widespread errors in values and gradients on CPU and GPU. Among scalar families in ordinary parameter ranges, over 85% of FP32 values have at least 1% relative error near KL 10^(-7) (FP16: 10^(-3)), and about 30% become negative at smaller divergences. More precision is not the cure: evaluated one precision higher, the same formulas still leave 7--51% of FP32 values significantly wrong for 22 of 23 configurations. Stable closed-form decompositions, compensated arithmetic, and analytic gradients remove over 97% of significant errors in the working format. Strict repairs eliminate significant errors on 7.2 million scored closed-form samples and correctly round all 567 million scored F.kl_div components. The errors affect parameter fitting, Bayesian decisions, identical-start distillation (up to 97% top-1 disagreement), KL-based layer rankings in a quantized LLM, and 19--59% of GPT-2 circuit edge scores. With the repaired code they all but vanish. Code and data: https://github.com/xi-xiaoran/stablekl
core_methodology: The paper focuses on improving the accuracy and stability of KL divergence calculations in PyTorch, addressing silent failures and numerical instability issues that affect machine learning applications using KL divergence.
data_sources: 18 closed-form KL families and F.kl_div evaluated on 8.5 million inputs with certified references.
alpha_potential: Improved KL divergence calculations could enhance parameter fitting, Bayesian decisions, and KL-based layer rankings in quantized models, which could indirectly benefit trading strategies that rely on Bayesian optimization, reinforcement learning, or other ML techniques.
title_cn: KL 散度从不为负，除非在 PyTorch 中
summary_cn: 该论文解决了 PyTorch 中 KL 散度计算不准确的问题，提出了稳定的分解形式、补偿算术和分析梯度，显著减少了计算误差。对于依赖 KL 散度的机器学习应用（如参数拟合、贝叶斯决策或 KL 层排序）的量化交易策略可能具有间接价值。

title: Variable Importance Recovery in Tabular Foundation Models: A Simulation Study
summary: In machine learning, identifying which variables contribute predictive information can be as important as predictive accuracy. Tabular foundation models have matched or exceeded the predictive performance of tuned gradient boosting trees on many small- and medium-sized tabular datasets. Yet their ability to recover population-level variable importance has received little attention. We design and conduct a Monte Carlo simulation study to compare variable importance recovery across tabular foundation models and established machine learning baselines. Our framework distinguishes multiple population estimands, pairs each one with an aligned model-agnostic importance estimator, and evaluates recovery in terms of ranking, support, and relative magnitude. Our results show that tabular foundation models are generally competitive with established machine-learning baselines in recovering population variable importance, and often more accurate. We thus extend the evidence for their capabilities to a previously underexamined dimension, further strengthening their appeal.
core_methodology: The paper employs Monte Carlo simulation studies to evaluate the ability of tabular foundation models to recover population-level variable importance compared to established machine learning baselines. The methodology includes distinguishing multiple population estimands and pairing each with model-agnostic importance estimators to evaluate recovery in terms of ranking, support, and relative magnitude.
data_sources: The study is based on small- and medium-sized tabular datasets, though specific financial datasets are not mentioned. The methodology could be applied to financial datasets for variable importance analysis.
alpha_potential: The ability to accurately recover variable importance can enhance feature selection in quantitative trading models, potentially leading to more robust signals. This could improve strategies like factor investing or portfolio optimization by better identifying predictive variables.
title_cn: 表格基础模型中的变量重要性恢复：仿真研究
summary_cn: 本研究通过蒙特卡洛仿真比较了表格基础模型与传统机器学习方法在恢复变量重要性方面的表现。研究结果表明，表格基础模型在恢复变量重要性方面具有竞争力，甚至更优。这一方法可应用于金融数据的特征选择，可能提升量化交易模型的预测性能。

title: Directional Bias in Quantile SGD and Score-Inversion Inference under Dependence
summary: Quantile stochastic gradient descent (SGD) tracks a quantile by comparing each observation with an adaptive threshold, and closely related updates calibrate online conformal sets and drive quantile temporal-difference learning. Their inputs are serially dependent, yet existing guarantees largely assume independence. We show that dependence creates a directional bias that score autocovariances cannot detect: reversing a stationary stream leaves every score autocovariance unchanged but can change the leading bias threefold. For finite memory and decreasing stepsizes, the bias splits into lag-specific interactions between the threshold and the current observation and a curvature term; delaying the threshold removes the interactions one lag at a time while keeping every observation and the leading variance. At stepsizes near $t^{-1/2}$, as used for online inference, the bias is comparable to the standard error and makes an SGD-based interval miss mostly on one side. Testing fixed candidates instead keeps the score centered, so calibration depends only on score autocovariances. Extending local-dependence self-normalized approximations to the implemented acceptance hull, we show that inverting these tests gives a density-free, moment-free interval for the population quantile with $O(n^{-1/2})$ coverage error for a fixed sufficient lag window, a rate that is sharp for this interval, and a guarantee for data-selected windows; an exact scan takes $O(n\log n)$ time. Experiments confirm the lag-by-lag predictions and show calibration competitive with block bootstrap at lower cost.
core_methodology: Quantile SGD for tracking quantiles and online conformal sets under serial dependence, with analysis of directional bias and lag-specific interactions.
data_sources: Serially dependent observations, typical in financial time series data.
alpha_potential: Potential for improving quantile-based trading strategies by accounting for directional bias and dependence in financial data, which could enhance risk management and signal generation.

title: Twisted Block Particle Filters: A Local Particle-System Change of Measure for High-Dimensional State-Space Models
summary: Block particle filters mitigate weight degeneracy in high-dimensional state-space models, but their normalizer estimates can remain highly variable. We introduce a twisted block particle filter (TBPF) that incorporates predictive guidance through an exact change of measure at blockwise resampling. The method guide-tilts one uniformly selected offspring per block, leaves the state-transition kernel unchanged, and computes the resampling correction using finite empirical guide averages. We prove that this correction exactly preserves the finite-particle block particle filter normalizer expectation, separating the effect of guided sampling from the approximation introduced by spatial blocking. Our analysis provides exact conditional local moments and a one-step conditional central limit result. We further derive explicit bounds on the correction accumulated across blocks and time, establish fixed-horizon consistency of the block filter and corrected normalizer under suitable regularity and guide-range conditions, and identify conditional criteria for guide perturbations that reduce variance. Experiments on coupled linear Gaussian and stochastic-volatility models with up to 256 latent dimensions show lower measured log-normalizer variance. For stochastic volatility with a five-step guide, the median reduction is $38\%$. An application to a 100-dimensional financial portfolio panel extends the evaluation to real data.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a twisted block particle filter (TBPF) that incorporates predictive guidance through an exact change of measure at blockwise resampling. This method aims to reduce the variability of normalizer estimates in high-dimensional state-space models, which is critical for accurate filtering in financial applications like stochastic volatility modeling.
data_sources: The paper evaluates the method on synthetic data (coupled linear Gaussian and stochastic-volatility models) and real-world financial data (100-dimensional financial portfolio panel).
alpha_potential: The TBPF's ability to reduce log-normalizer variance by up to 38% in stochastic volatility models suggests potential improvements in volatility estimation and risk management strategies, which are crucial for options pricing and portfolio optimization.
title_cn: 扭曲块粒子滤波器：高维状态空间模型的局部粒子系统测度变换
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种扭曲块粒子滤波器（TBPF），通过在块重采样时引入预测指导，显著降低了高维状态空间模型中归一化估计的方差。在金融应用中，这种方法可改进波动率建模，对期权定价和组合风险管理具有潜在价值。实验显示，该方法在256维潜在空间模型中能将对数归一化方差中值降低38%。

title: Sub-Gaussian HDLSS Principal Component Analysis: High-Probability Theory and Numerical Evidence for NRM, CDM, and Block Noise Reduction
summary: We study principal component analysis when the dimension d is much larger than the sample size n under an independent-factor sub-Gaussian model. The dual sample covariance is decomposed into a finite-rank score matrix, an isotropic bulk shift, and a high-probability remainder governed by the bulk trace \tau_0, Frobenius scale q_0, and largest noise eigenvalue b_0 = ||\Lambda_0||_{op}. This decomposition separates fixed-score HDLSS limits from joint limits in which n also grows. It shows that sequential noise reduction generally targets a score oracle containing a later-spike subtraction, while an oracle block correction avoids that subtraction when the signal rank is known. A parallel cross-data-matrix bound explains the benefit and cost of sample splitting. Reproducible Gaussian-factor simulations with 1,000 replications per configuration confirm the score-oracle approximation, the multi-spike subtraction, the separation between eigenvalue and eigenvector scales, and the population transition when n grows.
core_methodology: The paper presents a decomposition of the dual sample covariance matrix in high-dimension-low-sample-size (HDLSS) scenarios under a sub-Gaussian model. It focuses on principal component analysis (PCA) with sequential noise reduction and block correction methods to isolate signals from noise.
data_sources: Simulated data with Gaussian-factor models, as indicated by the reproducible experiments with 1,000 replications per configuration.

title: A Closed-Form Soft Spectral Partition for Adaptive Mode Decomposition
summary: Density-based Adaptive Mode Decomposition (DAMD) shows that the Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) objective, restricted to hard binary partitions, is equivalent to weighted K-means clustering, enabling automatic mode detection. The equivalence concerns detection only; extraction with hard Voronoi masks introduces boundary artefacts. This paper develops a soft extraction theory independent of the detector. First, the hard-partition equivalence is shown to be an algebraic identity that holds if and only if the weights are binary; hard and soft extraction are optima of two different functionals (linear K-means and regularised quadratic VMD) over the same simplex. Second, the regularised soft VMD problem is proved to have a closed-form global optimum, unique on the support of the spectrum: the Lorentzian-weighted partition $s_k^*(\omega)\propto[1+2\alpha(\omega-\omega_k)^2]^{-1}$. Every fixed point of the VMD ADMM mode update is proportional to $|\omega-\omega_k|^{-2}$; when the dual ascent enforces reconstruction, it is the $\alpha\to\infty$ endpoint of this family. The Lorentzian shape at finite $\alpha$ is therefore a consequence of the regulariser, and $\alpha$ controls how closely the allocation approaches that fixed point. Third, under a Lorentzian spectral prior the partition equals the minimum mean-square error (MMSE) estimator of each mode in the low-noise limit, tying $\alpha$ to the inverse squared mode bandwidth. Since the partition needs only detected centre frequencies, the extraction rule can be switched without recomputing detection. Synthetic experiments with known ground truth test the predictions; four categories of real signals show how much the two allocations differ.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a soft extraction theory for Adaptive Mode Decomposition (DAMD), which improves upon Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) by using Lorentzian-weighted partitions. This method provides a closed-form global optimum for mode extraction, reducing boundary artefacts present in hard-partition methods.
data_sources: The paper mentions synthetic experiments and four categories of real signals, but specific financial data types are not detailed. Potentially applicable to market data like price series, volatility, or other time-series financial data.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted to improve signal extraction in financial time-series analysis, particularly in decomposing complex market data into interpretable modes for trading strategies. The closed-form solution may enhance computational efficiency.
title_cn: 一种用于自适应模态分解的闭合形式软谱分割方法
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种基于Lorentzian加权分割的自适应模态分解方法，改进了传统VMD的边界伪影问题。该方法在金融时间序列分析中具有潜在应用价值，可用于分解复杂的市场数据，提高信号提取的效率和准确性。

title: Tabular Foundation Models for Weighted Regression and Classification
summary: Weighted regression and classification have applications ranging from missing-data analysis and causal inference to insurance pricing and particle physics. Existing weighted methods must be fitted and tuned on each dataset, which is costly for flexible nonlinear learners. Tabular foundation models avoid this cost. A Transformer is pretrained once on many simulated datasets and then predicts on a new dataset by in-context learning, using its observations as context without further fitting. Recent models such as TabPFN-3.5 surpass tuned conventional methods, but they cannot use sample weights. We develop a general pipeline that adapts such models to weighted prediction through weighted attention, a normalized weighted loss, and pretraining on synthetic weighted prediction tasks from missing-data problems. Applied to TabPFN-3.5, it yields WeightedPFN, which performs strongly on real datasets, both in missing-data problems and in out-of-distribution causal tasks, while running about as fast as linear baselines. We also establish a statistical theory showing that a suitably pretrained weighted Transformer attains the nonparametric minimax rate for weighted regression on new datasets without further fitting.
core_methodology: The paper introduces WeightedPFN, an adaptation of the TabPFN-3.5 transformer model, which incorporates weighted attention and a normalized weighted loss to handle weighted regression and classification tasks. The model is pretrained on synthetic datasets derived from missing-data problems and leverages in-context learning for prediction on new datasets without additional fitting.
data_sources: The model is pretrained on simulated datasets, which can include synthetic financial data scenarios such as missing-data problems or causal inference tasks. Real-world application is demonstrated on datasets that could include financial pricing or risk assessment data.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted for financial applications such as insurance pricing, risk assessment, or handling missing financial data. The ability to perform well on out-of-distribution tasks suggests potential for robust performance in changing market conditions.

summary_cn: 该论文开发了WeightedPFN，一种基于Transformer的表格基础模型，通过加权注意力和标准化加权损失处理加权回归和分类问题。模型在金融领域的潜在应用包括保险定价和风险评估，尤其在处理缺失数据和分布外任务时表现出色。

title: Robust Mixture Regressions and EM Algorithms via the Log-Truncated Likelihood
summary: Finite mixture regression is sensitive to gross residual outliers when component errors are modeled by Gaussian likelihoods. We propose a log-truncated likelihood for mixture regression. The likelihood is obtained by integrating a logarithmically growing Catoni-type score and exponentiating the negative integrated score, producing a proper location-scale density with a reusable normalizing constant and EM-compatible responsibilities. Although the induced density itself is lighter than exponential and has all moments, its likelihood score grows only logarithmically; this distinction yields a smooth residual-robust estimator that can be stably fitted when the data are generated from Laplace, Pareto, or even infinite-variance heavy-tailed error mechanisms. We derive deterministic tail envelopes, the location-scale decomposition of the normalizing constant, a rejection sampler, a lower-bounded mixing-weight update, a unique componentwise scale update, and a constrained generalized EM algorithm. The theory gives monotonicity of the observed likelihood and a local population-to-sample perturbation guarantee under standard compactness, contraction, and numerical-accuracy conditions. Simulations and applications to insurance claim severity and crypto return innovations show that the method is a competitive smooth likelihood-based alternative to Gaussian and pseudo-robust EM procedures, especially in residual-outlier regimes, while also clarifying its limitations under high leverage and extremely adversarial contamination.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a robust mixture regression model using a log-truncated likelihood, which is designed to handle gross residual outliers and heavy-tailed error mechanisms. It includes a constrained generalized EM algorithm for fitting the model.
data_sources: The paper mentions applications to insurance claim severity and crypto return innovations, suggesting it can be applied to financial data including cryptocurrency returns and insurance data.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be useful for developing robust trading strategies that are less sensitive to outliers, particularly in volatile markets like cryptocurrencies. The ability to handle heavy-tailed distributions may improve risk management and signal extraction.
