summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种基于对数截断似然的稳健混合回归方法，适用于处理金融数据中的极端异常值和厚尾分布。通过构建可约束的广义EM算法，该方法在保险索赔严重性和加密货币回报创新等应用中表现出色，为高频交易和风险管理提供了新的工具。

title: SpikeSTAG: A Dendritic Compartmental Spiking Graph Network for Multivariate Time-Series Forecasting
summary: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer a distinctive paradigm for temporal modeling through their intrinsic membrane potential dynamics. However, existing SNN-based forecasting methods focus exclusively on temporal processing, lacking mechanisms to capture spatial dependencies among variables. To bridge this gap, we propose SpikeSTAG, a neuromorphic spatiotemporal architecture that integrates graph-based spatial reasoning into spike-driven temporal computation. Central to our approach is the Dendritic Graph Module, which reinterprets spectral graph convolutions as biological dendritic integration --- coupling multi-scale spatial aggregation with the temporal dynamics of spiking neurons within a single computational unit. To adaptively fuse the resulting spatial and temporal representations, we further introduce a Dual-Stream Integration Module that employs competitive gating and coincidence-based amplification, selectively enhancing consistent spatiotemporal patterns while suppressing conflicting noise. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SpikeSTAG establishes a new state-of-the-art among SNN-based models and surpasses representative ANN baselines, while reducing theoretical energy consumption by approximately 66.7\% compared to Transformer architectures.
core_methodology: SpikeSTAG integrates spiking neural networks (SNNs) with graph-based spatial reasoning for multivariate time-series forecasting. It uses a Dendritic Graph Module to couple spatial aggregation with temporal dynamics of spiking neurons, and a Dual-Stream Integration Module for adaptive fusion of spatiotemporal representations.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources, but the methodology is applicable to multivariate financial time-series data such as stock prices, trading volumes, or macroeconomic indicators.
alpha_potential: The model's ability to capture spatiotemporal dependencies in multivariate data could be leveraged for momentum or mean-reversion strategies by identifying consistent patterns across correlated assets. The energy efficiency of SNNs may also enable high-frequency applications.

title: Roundtable Policy: Confidence-Weighted-Consensus Aggregation Improves Multi-Agent-System Reasoning
summary: Multi-agent systems have demonstrated exceptional performance in downstream tasks beyond diverse single agent baselines. A growing body of work has explored ways to improve their reasoning and collaboration, from vote, debate, to complex interaction protocols. However, it still remains opaque why specific choice would be preferred in multi-agent systems. Inspired by the decision-making mechanism of democratic committees and The Society of Mind, we introduce Roundtable Policy, an inference-time reasoning framework for multi-agent systems that performs inference through the weighted consensus of multiple LLMs. Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate its that this approach significantly enhances reasoning in complex heterogeneous scientific tasks. Roundtable Policy emphasizes structured and interpretable inference rather than opaque convergence, while requires only black-box access and uniform procedures, making it broadly applicable to diverse multi-agent systems.
core_methodology: Roundtable Policy is a framework for multi-agent systems that leverages weighted consensus among multiple LLMs for inference. It focuses on structured and interpretable decision-making through black-box access and uniform procedures.
data_sources: The paper does not specify particular financial data sources but suggests the methodology is broadly applicable to diverse multi-agent systems, which could include financial data in trading contexts.
alpha_potential: The methodology could potentially enhance trading strategies by aggregating diverse LLM-generated signals in a structured manner, reducing individual model biases and improving decision-making robustness.

title: Improving Sample Complexity of Critic-Actor Algorithms
summary: There has been significant research activity on studying the theoretical convergence guarantees (both asymptotic and non-asymptotic) for actor-critic (AC) algorithms. In a couple of recent papers, two-timescale critic-actor algorithms have been proposed where the role of the actor and critic is reversed, resulting in the algorithm mimicking value iteration as opposed to policy iteration. Finite time analysis has been carried out for a two-timescale critic-actor (CA) algorithm with function approximation and a sample complexity of $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-(2+\delta)})$ is obtained for some $\delta>0$ that is a function of the separation between the two step sizes. In this paper, we obtain improved sample complexity of $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-2})$ that had previously been achieved only by the single-timescale actor-critic algorithm. We propose modified learning rates for the actor and critic recursions that result in the improved sample complexity of the algorithm. This we obtain after weakening a key assumption in prior work. The sample complexity we obtain is the best so far reported in the literature for any multi-scale actor-critic or critic-actor algorithm. While the single-timescale actor-critic algorithm also achieves this sample complexity, it has been pointed out in prior work that this algorithm is not guaranteed to be asymptotically stable almost surely unlike our algorithm since we use a timescale separation for the critic and the actor. We additionally fully perform a finite-time analysis of the constrained natural critic-actor algorithm using the modified learning rates and also obtain a sample complexity bound of $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-2})$. We further show the results of experiments on different Gym and Safety-Gym environments where our algorithms are found to show good performance and are competitive in comparison to other well-known algorithms.
core_methodology: Two-timescale critic-actor algorithms with modified learning rates to achieve improved sample complexity.
data_sources: Gym and Safety-Gym environments (simulated data), though the methodology can be adapted to financial data.
alpha_potential: Potential for creating robust trading strategies via reinforcement learning with improved convergence properties, but requires adaptation to financial data.

title: Transformer Semantic Genetic Programming for d-dimensional Symbolic Regression Problems
summary: Transformer Semantic Genetic Programming (TSGP) is a semantic search approach that uses a pre-trained transformer model as a variation operator to generate offspring programs with high semantic similarity to a given parent. Unlike other semantic GP approaches that rely on fixed syntactic transformations, TSGP aims to learn diverse structural variations that lead to solutions with similar semantics. We find that a single transformer model trained on millions of programs is able to generalize across symbolic regression problems of varying dimensions. Evaluated on 24 real-world and synthetic datasets, TSGP significantly outperforms standard GP, SLIM_GSGP, Deep Symbolic Regression, and Denoising Autoencoder GP, achieving an average rank of 1.58 across all benchmarks. Moreover, TSGP produces more compact solutions than SLIM_GSGP, despite its higher accuracy. In addition, the target semantic distance is able to effectively adjust the step size in the semantic space: small values enable consistent improvement in fitness but often lead to larger programs, while larger values promote faster convergence and compactness. Thus, the target semantic distance provides an effective mechanism for balancing exploration and exploitation.
core_methodology: Transformer Semantic Genetic Programming (TSGP) uses a pre-trained transformer model as a variation operator to generate offspring programs with high semantic similarity to a given parent, focusing on symbolic regression problems.
data_sources: Evaluated on 24 real-world and synthetic datasets, but specific financial datasets are not mentioned.
alpha_potential: The method's ability to produce compact and accurate solutions could be adapted for developing trading signals or optimizing portfolio strategies, though direct financial application is not demonstrated.

title: Random-Bridges as Stochastic Transports for Generative Models
summary: This paper motivates the use of random-bridges -- stochastic processes conditioned to take target distributions at fixed timepoints -- in the realm of generative modelling. Herein, random-bridges act as stochastic transports between two probability distributions when appropriately initialized, displaying either Markovian or non-Markovian, and continuous, discontinuous, or hybrid patterns depending on the choice of the driving process. We show how one can start from general probabilistic statements and branch out into specific representations for learning and simulation algorithms. Essentially, our framework formulates stochastic transports as noisy information processes governing the dynamic translation and propagation of information between arbitrary probability measures. Our theoretical and algorithmic presentation details training and simulation frameworks for both Gaussian and L\'evy (specifically, Gamma, Poisson and Stable-$1/2$) random-bridge transports. The empirical validation focuses on the Gaussian case for demonstration and comparison purposes, where our construct delivers high-quality samples, achieving competitive Fr\'echet Inception Distance scores compared to widely used denoising diffusions and flow matching frameworks.
core_methodology: The paper introduces random-bridges as stochastic processes conditioned to take target distributions at fixed timepoints, used for generative modeling. These bridges act as stochastic transports between two probability distributions, with characteristics varying based on the driving process (Markovian/non-Markovian, continuous/discontinuous). The framework includes training and simulation for Gaussian and Lévy processes (Gamma, Poisson, Stable-1/2).
data_sources: The paper focuses on theoretical and algorithmic development, with empirical validation using synthetic data (Gaussian case). No specific financial market data is mentioned.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted for modeling financial time series or generating synthetic market data for stress testing or scenario analysis. However, direct alpha generation is not discussed.

title: Graph-based Nearest Neighbors with Dynamic Updates via Random Walks
summary: Approximate nearest neighbor search (ANN) is a common way to retrieve relevant search results, especially now in the context of large language models and retrieval augmented generation. One of the most widely used algorithms for ANN is based on constructing a multi-layer graph over the dataset, called the Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW). While this algorithm supports insertion of new data, it does not support deletion of existing data. Moreover, deletion algorithms described by prior work come at the cost of increased query latency, decreased recall, or prolonged deletion time. In this paper, we propose a new theoretical framework for graph-based ANN based on random walks. We then utilize this framework to analyze a randomized deletion approach that approximately preserves hitting time statistics compared to the graph before deleting the point. However, this guarantee needs at least as many edge samples as there are edges in the clique over the neighbors of the deleted point. We then turn this theoretical framework into a deterministic deletion algorithm, and show that it provides a better tradeoff between query latency, recall, deletion time, and memory usage through an extensive collection of experiments.
core_methodology: Graph-based approximate nearest neighbor search (ANN) with dynamic updates via random walks, focusing on a new theoretical framework for efficient deletion of data while preserving graph properties.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources but the methodology can be applied to any high-dimensional financial datasets such as asset price time series, order book data, or alternative data embeddings.
alpha_potential: Potential to improve real-time retrieval systems in trading strategies that rely on similarity search, such as pattern recognition in price series or portfolio optimization tasks requiring nearest neighbor lookups in high-dimensional factor spaces.

title: What If TSF: Evaluating Scenario-Guided Multimodal Time Series Forecasting
summary: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have enabled time series forecasting to move beyond numerical observations and incorporate external information in multimodal settings. Such information can improve forecasting performance, but accuracy alone may not reveal whether models appropriately respond to it: a model may ignore relevant information, fail to distinguish scenarios with different implications, or overreact to irrelevant or weak signals. We introduce What If TSF (WIT), a benchmark for evaluating whether models effectively respond to future scenarios. WIT constructs controlled scenario sets by fixing the forecasting state while systematically varying future scenarios, enabling three complementary evaluations: Factual Comparison, which measures the predictive utility of factual scenario information; Relational Comparison, which evaluates whether forecasts satisfy expected direction, contrast, intensity, and restraint relations across scenarios; and Grounded Comparison, which provides a complementary empirical assessment of scenario-induced revision trajectories where comparable real cases are available. Experiments show that factual accuracy gains do not consistently translate into appropriate responses to alternative scenarios, demonstrating the need to evaluate multimodal forecasting beyond predictive accuracy.
core_methodology: The paper introduces What If TSF (WIT), a benchmark for evaluating multimodal time series forecasting models by constructing controlled scenario sets. It focuses on three evaluations: Factual Comparison, Relational Comparison, and Grounded Comparison to assess model responses to future scenarios.
data_sources: The paper likely uses multimodal data, combining numerical time series with external information (possibly text from LLMs) to construct scenario sets for forecasting.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted to financial markets by incorporating scenario-guided forecasts. For example, using LLMs to interpret news or macroeconomic scenarios and evaluate their impact on asset prices. The ability to distinguish relevant from irrelevant scenarios could help in filtering noise from signals.

title: Efficient Adaptive Data Analysis over Dense Data Distributions
summary: Modern data workflows are inherently adaptive, repeatedly querying the same dataset to refine and validate sequential decisions, but such adaptivity can lead to overfitting and invalid statistical inference. Adaptive Data Analysis (ADA) mechanisms address this challenge; however, there is a fundamental tension between computational efficiency and sample complexity. For $T$ rounds of adaptive analysis, computationally efficient algorithms typically incur suboptimal $O(\sqrt{T})$ sample complexity, whereas for arbitrary distributions, algorithms with $O(\log T)$ sample complexity are computationally intractable under standard cryptographic assumptions. In this work, we shed light on this trade-off by identifying a natural class of data distributions under which both computational efficiency and logarithmic sample complexity in $T$ are achievable. We propose a computationally efficient ADA mechanism that attains $O(\log T)$ sample complexity, optimal in its dependence on $T$, when the data distribution is dense with respect to a known prior. This setting includes, in particular, feature-label data distributions arising in distribution-specific learning. As a consequence, our mechanism also yields a sample-efficient (i.e., $O(\log T)$ samples) statistical query oracle in the distribution-specific setting. Moreover, although our algorithm is not based on differential privacy, it satisfies a relaxed privacy notion known as Predicate Singling Out (PSO) security (Cohen and Nissim 2020) whenever the number of its possible update transcripts is polynomial in the sample size. Our results thus reveal an inherent connection between adaptive data analysis and privacy beyond differential privacy.
core_methodology: The paper introduces an Adaptive Data Analysis (ADA) mechanism that achieves computational efficiency and logarithmic sample complexity for dense data distributions. This method is particularly relevant for handling feature-label distributions in data-driven learning scenarios.
data_sources: The paper does not specify particular financial datasets but implies applicability to any dense data distributions, which could include market data, feature-label pairs in quantitative models, or other financial time series data.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be leveraged to improve the efficiency of adaptive trading strategies that rely on sequential data analysis, such as high-frequency trading or dynamic portfolio optimization. The logarithmic sample complexity suggests potential for reducing overfitting in adaptive models.

title: Towards Adaptive, Scalable, and Robust Coordination of LLM Agents: A Dynamic Ad-Hoc Networking Perspective
summary: Multi-agent architectures built on large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated the potential to realize swarm intelligence through well-crafted collaboration. However, the substantial burden of manual orchestration inherently raises an imperative to automate the design of agentic workflows. We frame such an agent coordination challenge as a classic problem in dynamic ad-hoc networking: How to establish adaptive and reliable communication among a scalable number of agentic hosts? In response to this unresolved dilemma, we introduce RAPS, a reputation-aware publish-subscribe paradigm for adaptive, scalable, and robust coordination of LLM agents. RAPS is grounded in the Distributed Publish-Subscribe Protocol, allowing LLM agents to exchange messages based on their declared intents rather than predefined topologies. Beyond this substrate, RAPS further incorporates two coherent overlays: (i) Reactive Subscription, enabling agents to dynamically refine their intents; and (ii) Bayesian Reputation, empowering each agent with a local watchdog to detect and isolate malicious peers. Extensive experiments over five benchmarks showcase that our design effectively reconciles adaptivity, scalability, and robustness in a unified multi-agent coordination framework.
core_methodology: Reputation-aware publish-subscribe paradigm (RAPS) for adaptive, scalable, and robust coordination of LLM agents, incorporating Reactive Subscription and Bayesian Reputation overlays.
data_sources: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be general multi-agent communication benchmarks.
alpha_potential: Potential for optimizing multi-agent trading systems by improving coordination and robustness, though not directly applied to financial data or markets.

summary_cn: 该论文提出了RAPS，一种基于声誉感知的发布-订阅范式，用于优化LLM智能体的自适应、可扩展和鲁棒协调。虽然未直接涉及金融应用，但其方法论可能为多智能体交易系统的优化提供参考。

title: Actor-Accelerated Policy Dual Averaging for Reinforcement Learning in Continuous Action Spaces
summary: Policy Dual Averaging (PDA) offers a principled Policy Mirror Descent (PMD) framework that more naturally admits value function approximation than standard PMD, enabling the use of approximate advantage (or Q-) functions while retaining strong convergence guarantees. However, applying PDA in continuous state and action spaces remains computationally challenging, since action selection involves solving an optimization subproblem at each decision step. In this paper, we propose \textit{actor-accelerated PDA} (AA-PDA), which uses a learned policy network to approximate the solution of the optimization subproblems, significantly reducing runtime. We provide a theoretical analysis that quantifies how actor approximation error impacts the convergence of PDA under suitable assumptions. We then evaluate its performance on several benchmarks in robotics, control, and operations research problems. AA-PDA achieves better performance compared to on-policy baselines such as Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). Overall, our results take a step toward bridging the gap between the theoretical advantages of PDA and its practical deployment in continuous-action problems with function approximation. Our code is available at https://github.com/jgioa/pdarl
core_methodology: Actor-Accelerated Policy Dual Averaging (AA-PDA) is a reinforcement learning method that combines Policy Dual Averaging (PDA) with a learned policy network to approximate the solution of optimization subproblems, thereby reducing computational complexity in continuous action spaces.
data_sources: The paper evaluates the method on benchmarks in robotics, control, and operations research, but does not specify financial market data.
alpha_potential: The method's ability to handle continuous action spaces efficiently could be adapted for high-frequency trading or portfolio optimization problems where action spaces are continuous. The theoretical guarantees on convergence with function approximation may provide robustness in dynamic trading environments.
title_cn: 连续动作空间中强化学习的演员加速策略双重平均方法
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种演员加速策略双重平均（AA-PDA）方法，通过结合策略双重平均（PDA）与学习策略网络，有效降低了连续动作空间中的计算复杂度。虽然本文未直接涉及金融市场应用，但其方法在高效处理连续动作空间方面的优势可潜在应用于高频交易或投资组合优化等场景。

title: Informed Machine Learning with Knowledge Landmarks
summary: Informed Machine Learning (ML) aims to improve prediction by using both data and prior knowledge. In scientific and engineering applications, accurate measurements may occupy only a small operating region of the input space, whereas available knowledge is global, coarse, and not expressed as equations. Existing physics-informed methods embed governing equations, residuals, simulators, operators, or mathematically specified constraints. However, they do not directly address learning from localized numeric data together with non-equational knowledge. We develop a Knowledge-Data (KD) ML framework for this setting. The KD-model represents coarse global knowledge as input-output information granules, termed knowledge landmarks. The method uses a landmark-guided objective that converts these landmarks into differentiable compatibility terms and balances them against local data fitting through a trade-off parameter $\lambda$. Experiments on two physics-based benchmarks show that the KD-model predicts more accurately across the full domain than a model trained on the local data alone. For most observation windows, the gain holds over a broad range of $\lambda$. The advantage persists when the sample size or label noise changes, with $\lambda$ re-selected without full-domain labels. These results show that approximate expert knowledge can guide training when dense labels or explicit equations are unavailable.
core_methodology: The paper presents a Knowledge-Data (KD) Machine Learning framework that integrates coarse global knowledge (expressed as input-output information granules or knowledge landmarks) with localized numeric data. The method uses a landmark-guided objective to balance these knowledge landmarks against local data fitting, optimizing via a trade-off parameter λ.
data_sources: The abstract mentions experiments on two physics-based benchmarks, but specific data sources for financial applications are not detailed. Potential financial applications could use market data combined with expert knowledge (e.g., macroeconomic indicators, trading rules of thumb).
alpha_potential: This methodology could be valuable in quantitative finance for scenarios where expert knowledge (e.g., market regimes, risk preferences) is available but not easily quantifiable. It may improve predictions in sparse data regimes or enhance model generalization by incorporating domain expertise.
title_cn: 基于知识地标的知情机器学习
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种知识数据（KD）机器学习框架，通过将全局专家知识（以输入-输出信息粒或知识地标的形式）与本地数值数据结合，优化模型预测。在量化交易中，该方法可用于融合市场经验规则与高频数据，提升稀疏数据下的预测性能或在复杂市场环境中增强模型泛化能力。

title: The Limits of Behavioral Early Warning for Copy-Trading Blow-Ups: A Pre-Registered, Full-Universe On-Chain Study (Hyperliquid)
summary: A common, rarely-tested assumption behind copy-trading risk controls is that "behavioral monitoring catches blow-ups": that a master trader's conduct drifts before the equity damage that wipes out followers. We test this on real on-chain money over the full public Hyperliquid leaderboard: 37,895 addresses, filtered to 10,395 "master-worth-copying" accounts, yielding 2,621 genuine loss-driven idiosyncratic blow-ups across 48 independent crash-days. On a model-free panel of 2,477 blow-up masters, behavioral drift leads equity for only 9% (216 masters); 69% blow up with no gradual behavioral signal at all, and the overall median lead is negative (-8 days): when conduct moves, it typically lags the equity rather than leading it. A purpose-built three-axis mixture-SPRT detector, pre-registered with its operating point frozen on a disjoint tuning split and read once against a sealed test set, confirms the boundary rather than beating it: it achieves chance-level discrimination (AUC 0.49) at 2% recall. It does post the lowest false-positive rate of any method (0.040, ~1.9x below a leverage tripwire), but at negligible recall that precision is of little practical use. Behavioral early warning is therefore not a viable general safety net for copy-trading blow-ups: most are sudden, a plain equity / drawdown stop fires as early on them, and the residual behavioral signal (gradual over-leveraging) precedes fewer than one blow-up in ten.
core_methodology: The paper employs a model-free panel analysis and a purpose-built three-axis mixture-SPRT detector to test the effectiveness of behavioral monitoring in predicting copy-trading blow-ups. The methodology involves a pre-registered, full-universe on-chain study with real money data.
data_sources: The study uses real on-chain money data from the full public Hyperliquid leaderboard, encompassing 37,895 addresses, filtered to 10,395 "master-worth-copying" accounts, yielding 2,621 genuine loss-driven idiosyncratic blow-ups across 48 independent crash-days.
alpha_potential: The paper identifies that behavioral early warning is not a viable general safety net for copy-trading blow-ups, as most blow-ups are sudden and behavioral signals lag equity damage. This suggests that traditional equity/drawdown stops may be more effective, providing a potential area for optimization in risk management strategies.
title_cn: 行为早期预警在跟单交易爆仓中的局限性：一项预注册、全宇宙链上研究（Hyperliquid）

title: Political Orientation and Participation in Prediction Markets: Large Stakes Converge, Small Stakes Diverge
summary: Prediction markets offer a way to study collective expectations and beliefs: people express their views on various events and, by putting money behind their predictions, take on the risks of their judgments. As a result, the scale of investment can reveal additional dimensions of individual behavior and beliefs. In this study, we use a complex network approach to examine the structure of user participation, drawing on roughly 1.14 billion transaction records from the Polymarket platform, covering more than 3.1 million wallet addresses and 764,000 prediction events. To do this, we build a bipartite network of users and events and analyze patterns of investment concentration, connections between topics, and the network's community structure. Our findings show a highly skewed distribution of financial participation: 1\% of events account for 64\% of total transaction volume, while 1\% of wallets account for 79.2\% of total financial participation. We also examine how investment scale and political orientation shape user participation patterns. Focusing on the 2024 U.S. presidential election, we compare users who invested exclusively in a Trump victory or exclusively in a Harris victory, grouping wallets by purchase size rather than by retail or institutional status. The results show that among large-scale investors, capital allocation patterns across topics are more similar between the two political groups; in contrast, these patterns diverge more and vary more among small-scale investors. This result holds across six different ways of representing and comparing the networks, and four of these differences are also statistically supported.
core_methodology: Complex network analysis of user participation in prediction markets, focusing on investment concentration and political orientation.
data_sources: 1.14 billion transaction records from the Polymarket platform, covering 3.1 million wallet addresses and 764,000 prediction events.
alpha_potential: Potential insights into collective behavior and political bias in market predictions, which could be leveraged for sentiment analysis or contrarian strategies.
title_cn: 政治倾向与预测市场参与：大额趋同，小额分歧
summary_cn: 本研究通过复杂网络分析预测市场中的用户参与模式，揭示了大规模投资者在政治相关事件上的资本分配趋同，而小额投资者则表现出较大分歧。这对量化交易中的市场情绪分析和政治事件驱动的策略设计有一定参考价值。

title: Tight Mistake-Abstention Tradeoffs for Sequential Prediction under Adversarial Injections
summary: We study the sequential prediction problem introduced by Goel et al. (2023), where an adversary can inject arbitrarily many corrupted instances in an i.i.d. stream from a clean distribution $\mu$, while the learner is allowed to abstain from making a prediction at no cost if the current instance was indeed injected. When $\mu$ is unknown, Yu and Blanchard (2026) show a polynomial tradeoff between mistakes and false abstentions for classes with finite VC dimension and oblivious adversaries, but still leave open a significant gap between upper and lower bounds in their tradeoff landscape. In this paper, we propose the weighted shattering potential, and based on variants of this potential, provide gap-closing algorithms that essentially characterize the tradeoffs under various settings of interest: When $\mu$ is known, our algorithm improves over Goel et al. (2023) and achieves their conjectured $O(d\log T)$ mistake bound; When $\mu$ is unknown, for oblivious adversary, our guarantees are tight both in $T$ and in terms of the VC dimension $d$, which completely characterizes the abstention-mistake tradeoff in this setting and gives an $O(\sqrt{dT})$ balanced rate. For adaptive adversary, our results are tight up to $\operatorname{poly}(dD\log T)$ factors for structured classes with finite so-called reduction dimension $D$. Our guarantees also extend to censored feedback, where the label is hidden after an abstention.
core_methodology: The paper introduces the weighted shattering potential and its variants to address the sequential prediction problem with adversarial injections. It provides algorithms that achieve tight tradeoffs between mistakes and false abstentions, particularly for settings where the clean distribution is known or unknown, and for various types of adversaries (oblivious or adaptive).
data_sources: The methodology is abstract and not tied to specific market data, but it could theoretically be applied to financial time series or order book data where adversarial injections (e.g., spoofing or wash trading) may occur.
alpha_potential: The paper's approach could potentially be adapted to detect adversarial manipulations in financial markets, such as identifying spoofing or other forms of market abuse. However, the direct application to generate alpha is unclear without further empirical validation in financial contexts.

title: A Polynomial-Time Best-of-Both-Worlds Algorithm for Matroid Semi-Bandit Problems
summary: Follow-the-Perturbed-Leader (FTPL) offers a computationally attractive framework for online learning, with recent advances establishing Best-of-Both-Worlds (BOBW) guarantees for various bandit settings. For matroid semi-bandits, existing methods offering such guarantees primarily rely on Follow-the-Regularized-Leader (FTRL), which requires solving an optimization problem at each round. We establish BOBW guarantees for FTPL with Fr\'echet and Pareto distributions with a certain parameter with geometric resampling in the matroid semi-bandit problem, showing that FTPL can simultaneously achieve the minimax-optimal $O(\sqrt{mdT})$ regret in adversarial setting and a logarithmic regret in stochastic setting. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first polynomial-time algorithm for matroid semi-bandits that achieves BOBW guarantees.
core_methodology: Follow-the-Perturbed-Leader (FTPL) algorithm applied to matroid semi-bandit problems, achieving Best-of-Both-Worlds guarantees with Fréchet and Pareto distributions using geometric resampling.
data_sources: Primarily theoretical, no specific financial data sources mentioned, but adaptable to market data.
alpha_potential: Potential application in online portfolio optimization and adaptive trading strategies where decision-making under uncertainty is critical.
title_cn: 一种多项式时间的两全其美算法用于拟阵半强盗问题
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种基于‘跟随扰动领导者’（FTPL）的多项式时间算法，用于拟阵半强盗问题，同时在对抗环境和随机环境中实现最优的后悔界。该方法可应用于在线投资组合优化和自适应交易策略，尤其在不确定市场中表现得更加稳健。核心创新是采用几何重采样与Fréchet和Pareto分布，显著降低了计算复杂度。

title: SGPC: Safety-Guiding Policy Constraint for Stable Off-Policy Safe Reinforcement Learning
summary: Off-policy safe reinforcement learning (RL) faces a challenging trade-off between task optimality and constraint feasibility. In primal-dual methods, the coupled optimization of cumulative reward and constraint penalties through adaptive Lagrange multipliers may induce oscillatory policy updates near the safety boundary and amplify the effect of unreliable reward estimates outside the safe set. To address these issues, we formulate a new constrained optimization problem (COP) for safe RL by introducing a Safety-Guiding Policy (SGP) and a corresponding Safety-Guiding Policy Constraint (SGPC). The proposed COP augments the standard COP in safe RL with a conditional safety-guidance constraint. During actor updates, the current actor is evaluated using the learned cost critic. If it is predicted to be outside the safe set, SGP provides a nearby lower-cost training reference, and SGPC guides actor optimization toward this reference. Once the policy enters the safe set, the added constraint becomes inactive, and the formulation reduces to the original COP. This formulation leads to a plug-in actor-training constraint that can be integrated into off-policy safe RL algorithms. By applying primal-dual optimization to the auxiliary COP, we finally derive an SGPC-based off-policy safe RL algorithm and implement it in two representative off-policy algorithms, yielding SAC-SGPC and TD3-SGPC. Experiments on multiple Safety-Gymnasium benchmarks demonstrate that SGPC achieves a better optimality-safety trade-off by substantially reducing constraint violations and cost oscillations while maintaining competitive or better task returns.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a Safety-Guiding Policy Constraint (SGPC) for off-policy safe Reinforcement Learning (RL), which aims to balance task optimality and constraint feasibility by using a safety-guiding policy to provide lower-cost references during actor updates.
data_sources: The paper uses Safety-Gymnasium benchmarks, which are simulation environments designed for safe RL testing, not real-world financial data.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted to trading strategies where safety constraints (e.g., risk limits, drawdown control) are critical, potentially improving the stability of RL-based trading algorithms in volatile markets.
title_cn: SGPC：稳定离策略安全强化学习的安全引导策略约束
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种安全引导策略约束（SGPC）方法，用于离策略安全强化学习（RL），旨在通过安全引导策略在演员更新期间提供低成本参考，平衡任务最优性和约束可行性。该方法可潜在应用于需要严格控制风险的量化交易策略，提高RL算法在波动市场中的稳定性。

title: From Rewarding What Models Say to How They Think: Attention Process Reward Model for LLM Reinforcement Learning
summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become an important component in large language models (LLMs). However, existing RL approaches focus on final outputs or textual solution trajectories, leading to coarse-grained rewards and unreliable reasoning. Such paradigms focus mainly on what the model outputs while overlooking how the model internally reasons. Therefore, can we reward how a model thinks internally rather than merely what it says? We first reveal the problem of textual reward aliasing in existing reward modeling approaches. Motivated by this, we propose the Attention Process Reward Model (APRM), which assigns internal rewards based on hidden states and attention maps to capture high-quality reasoning patterns. With only approximately 46M parameters, APRM is trained using ranking and counterfactual objectives, and its reward guides RL optimization while being periodically updated to handle distribution shifts. Integrated with representative RL methods, APRM achieved an average pass@8 gain of 2.88\%. Our results demonstrate the promise of incorporating internal reasoning signals into RL for LLMs.
core_methodology: The paper introduces an Attention Process Reward Model (APRM) that utilizes hidden states and attention maps from LLMs to provide fine-grained rewards based on internal reasoning patterns, rather than just final outputs. This is applied in reinforcement learning to improve the quality of LLM reasoning.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources, but the methodology could theoretically be applied to text or structured financial data processed by LLMs.
alpha_potential: The methodology could potentially be adapted to improve reasoning in financial LLM applications, such as sentiment analysis, news interpretation, or report generation, by ensuring more reliable internal reasoning processes. However, the direct application to trading strategies is not demonstrated.

summary_cn: 本文提出了一种注意力过程奖励模型（APRM），通过隐藏状态和注意力图对LLM的内部推理过程进行细粒度奖励，以提高强化学习的效果。这种方法可能应用于金融领域的LLM推理任务，如新闻解读或报告生成，以确保更可靠的推理过程，但其在交易策略中的直接应用尚未验证。

title: Rewirable Circuits in Transformers with Loom Attention
summary: We propose loom attention, which allows a Transformer to dynamically rewire its circuits at every token by interweaving a head's vertical attention over the outputs of earlier heads (to obtain its query, key and value) with its horizontal attention over tokens. We instantiate vertical attention efficiently with normalized and gated linear attention over a per-token matrix memory, which stores the compressed head outputs and serves as a second residual stream. This yields LoomFormer, a dual-stream architecture that splits control and content between the vector and matrix streams. Across model sizes and training token budgets in language modeling and downstream tasks, LoomFormer matches Transformers trained with over 3x compute and recent residual-stream baselines (HC/mHC, MUDDFormer, AttnRes) trained with ~1.7-2.8x. For example, trained on the same 300B tokens with only 2% extra FLOPs, LoomPythia-2.8B achieves ~1.6x the average downstream gain of mHC-Pythia-2.8B over Pythia-2.8B, and matches (0-shot) or surpasses (5-shot) Pythia-12B. Code is available at https://github.com/Caiyun-AI/LoomFormer
core_methodology: Loom attention in Transformers allows dynamic rewiring of circuits at every token by interweaving vertical and horizontal attention, enabling a dual-stream architecture for improved efficiency and performance.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources, focusing instead on general language modeling tasks.
alpha_potential: The methodology could potentially be adapted to process sequential financial data more efficiently, offering improvements in speed and performance for time-series analysis and prediction tasks.

title: Continuous-Time LQR from a Single Discrete-Time Off-Policy Batch
summary: We study discounted continuous-time linear--quadratic regulation (LQR) with unknown drift parameters and additive noise, using a single batch of discrete-time off-policy transitions. Discrete-time methods target a policy tied to the training interval, while shortening this interval can make learning from finite data more sensitive to noise. Learning an accurate continuous-time controller therefore requires balancing discretization and finite-sample errors while preserving stability throughout policy improvement. We develop a drift-only policy iteration algorithm, termed PhiBE-PI, using one quadratic state--action critic for policy evaluation and explicit greedy improvement. Reusing the batch makes later policies depend on the data. Exploiting the quadratic structure of LQR, we show that the data enter every policy evaluation only through one policy-independent empirical matrix, so a single high-probability bound controls all iterates. For sufficiently large discount~$\beta$, small observation intervals, and a sufficiently large batch, we prove that all iterates are stabilizing for the discounted problem and converge quadratically to a data-dependent fixed point. The gain bound separates iteration, finite-sample, and discretization errors. In this regime, the finite-sample and discretization terms scale as $1/(\beta\sqrt{n\Delta t})$ and $\Delta t/\beta$, respectively. The bounds thus reveal a tradeoff: at a fixed batch size, finer observations reduce discretization error but increase finite-sample error. Because PhiBE-PI approximates the continuous-time optimal gain rather than a discrete-time one, its policy can remain near-optimal when deployed at faster control rates. Experiments confirm this advantage over discrete-time Bellman-equation baselines when the observation interval is small relative to the system's time scale.
core_methodology: The paper presents a drift-only policy iteration algorithm (PhiBE-PI) for continuous-time linear-quadratic regulation (LQR) using a single batch of discrete-time off-policy transitions. It focuses on balancing discretization and finite-sample errors while preserving stability throughout policy improvement.
data_sources: The methodology does not specify particular market data but assumes access to discrete-time state-action transitions, which could be derived from financial time series or trading data.
alpha_potential: Potential applications include dynamic portfolio optimization or algorithmic trading strategies where continuous-time control is beneficial. The method’s ability to approximate continuous-time optimal gains could lead to more stable and adaptive trading policies, especially in high-frequency trading scenarios.

summary_cn: 本文提出了一种基于单次离散时间离策批次的连续时间线性二次调节（LQR）方法，通过平衡离散化和有限样本误差来提升策略稳定性。该方法在金融交易中的潜在应用包括动态组合优化和高频交易策略，能够生成更稳定的连续时间控制策略。

title: Sharp Asymptotic Theory of Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Gaussian Processes with a Matern Kernel
summary: Gaussian processes (GPs) provide a flexible framework for modeling complex dependence structures through a covariance function, or kernel, whose parameters determine the variability, correlation, and smoothness of the underlying process. The Mat\'ern kernel is among the most popular choices due to its flexibility in modeling different degrees of smoothness. Although the identifiability of Mat\'ern kernel parameters under fixed-domain asymptotics is completely understood, identifiability alone does not establish the consistency or asymptotic behavior of the maximum likelihood estimators (MLEs) routinely used in practice. In this paper, we address this gap by developing a sharp asymptotic theory for the joint MLE of Mat\'ern kernel parameters. Since parameter identifiability depends critically on the dimension of the observation domain, we characterize the estimable parameters and establish their convergence rates across different dimensions. We establish joint asymptotic normality and minimax optimality of the convergence rates. In addition, we establish asymptotically valid confidence regions for the estimable parameters. Our results accommodate irregular sampling designs and extend to sub-Gaussian measurement errors. Extensive simulation studies illustrate the theoretical results.
core_methodology: Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) for Gaussian Processes (GPs) with a Matérn kernel, focusing on asymptotic theory for parameter estimation under fixed-domain asymptotics.
data_sources: Theoretical framework applicable to any time series or spatial data with complex dependence structures, can be adapted to financial time series.
alpha_potential: Potential for modeling and predicting financial time series with complex dependence structures, improving volatility or correlation estimates. Requires adaptation to financial contexts.
title_cn: 使用Matérn核的高斯过程最大似然估计的尖锐渐近理论
summary_cn: 本研究针对Matérn核的高斯过程提出了最大似然估计的尖锐渐近理论，为金融时间序列的复杂依赖结构建模提供了理论基础，可作为波动率或相关性估计的技术基础，需进一步结合金融场景适配。

title: Escaping Offline Pessimism: Vector-Field Reward Shaping for Safe Frontier Exploration
summary: While offline reinforcement learning provides reliable policies for real-world deployment, its inherent pessimism severely restricts an agent's ability to explore and collect novel data online. Drawing inspiration from safe reinforcement learning, exploring near the boundary of regions well covered by the offline dataset and reliably modeled by the simulator allows an agent to take manageable risks--venturing into informative but moderate-uncertainty states while remaining close enough to familiar regions for safe recovery. However, naively rewarding this boundary-seeking behavior can lead to a degenerate parking behavior, where the agent simply stops once it reaches the frontier. To solve this, we propose a novel vector-field reward shaping paradigm designed to induce continuous, safe boundary exploration for non-adaptive deployed policies. Operating on an uncertainty oracle trained from offline data, our reward combines two complementary components: a gradient-alignment term that attracts the agent toward a target uncertainty level, and a rotational-flow term that promotes motion along the local tangent plane of the uncertainty manifold. Through theoretical analysis, we show that this reward structure naturally induces sustained exploratory behavior along the boundary while preventing degenerate solutions. Empirically, by integrating our proposed reward shaping with Soft Actor-Critic on a 2D continuous navigation task, we validate that agents successfully traverse uncertainty boundaries while balancing safe, informative data collection with primary task completion.
core_methodology: Vector-field reward shaping for safe frontier exploration in reinforcement learning, combining gradient-alignment and rotational-flow terms to promote continuous exploration along uncertainty boundaries.
data_sources: Offline dataset and simulator for training the uncertainty oracle, though specifics are not mentioned.
alpha_potential: Potential for enhancing exploration in algorithmic trading strategies, particularly in risk-managed environments where balancing exploration and exploitation is crucial. The methodology could be adapted to discover new trading signals or optimize portfolio rebalancing strategies.

title: Measuring and Teaching Language Model Agents to Act on Delayed Consequences
summary: Language model agents are increasingly asked to run ongoing multi-day operations rather than finish isolated single-turn tasks. In daily operations, today's choices reshape later observations and cash constraints because empty shelves hide lost walk-in demand, short-shipped customers quietly shrink future orders weeks later, and emergency buying drains working capital. We introduce SMB Bench, a calibrated 90-day wholesale simulator with 18 causally paired tasks and an 859-run frontier trace dataset, to ask what experience and learning signal make an agent better at noticing, attributing, and acting on the delayed consequences of its own decisions in unseen businesses. Across 16 frontier models, only 3 outperform a fixed buying rule; models often record a relevant diagnosis in their notes without changing later purchases in time, showing that diagnosing a problem, changing behavior, and improving a business are separate achievements. To study how experience improves those failures in an open model (Qwen3.8-27B), we used training-business records to identify operational rules and archived frontier quarters as starting states to continue from rather than transcripts to copy. On an unseen test business under identical evaluation instructions, the trained policy followed customer-protection commitments more consistently and reduced severe-loss quarters, while the additional profit benefit remained uncertain. Carrying those commitments through the quarter exposed the cost of fulfilling them, as early-quarter stocking habits left the buyer relying on emergency supply and a deteriorating supplier. The results separate recognizing a delayed effect, acting on it consistently, and coordinating surrounding decisions so that the response improves profit. SMB Bench connects these observations to a learning method by turning archived decisions and their consequences into reusable training experience.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a simulator (SMB Bench) to study how language model agents can learn from delayed consequences of their decisions in wholesale operations. It evaluates the agents' ability to diagnose problems, change behavior, and improve business outcomes over a 90-day period.
data_sources: The paper uses a synthetic dataset (SMB Bench) consisting of an 859-run frontier trace dataset from a calibrated 90-day wholesale simulator with 18 causally paired tasks.
alpha_potential: The study highlights the challenge of agents recognizing and acting on delayed consequences, which could potentially be adapted to trading scenarios where actions have delayed market impacts. However, the direct application to quantitative trading is limited as the focus is on wholesale operations rather than financial markets.

title: torchtsetlin: Fast, Interpretable Tsetlin Machines for PyTorch
summary: The Tsetlin machine learns propositional rules with teams of Tsetlin automata that are driven by reward and penalty rather than gradients, so its models are interpretable by construction and cheap to evaluate. Its software, however, consists of C and CUDA kernels behind scikit-learn-style wrappers that sit outside the deep learning ecosystem. torchtsetlin implements the Tsetlin machine family as ordinary PyTorch modules: vanilla and weighted, coalesced, regression, convolutional over sequences, images and volumes, and dense per-pixel segmentation. The automata are a tensor buffer, so a model moves with .to(device), is saved with state_dict() and learns from a mini-batch with one update(x,y) call. Its core technique is a batched formulation of Type I and Type II feedback, in which automaton transitions become event counts realised as binomial draws, with one commit per mini-batch. On ten benchmarks taken from the existing libraries, it matches their accuracy, and on all but the two smallest it trains 2.4-10.9X faster than PyTsetlinMachineCUDA and 10.3-81.2X faster than tmu on the same GPU. The package is pure Python, MIT-licensed and on PyPI; every number in this paper is reproduced by one script. Code: https://github.com/vlbthambawita/torchtsetlin; package: https://pypi.org/project/torchtsetlin/.
core_methodology: Tsetlin machines learn propositional rules using Tsetlin automata driven by reward and penalty, offering interpretability and efficient computation. The implementation integrates with PyTorch, enabling models to leverage GPU acceleration and standard PyTorch workflows.
data_sources: Benchmark datasets from existing libraries (unspecified financial relevance).
alpha_potential: Potential for interpretable rule-based models in financial decision-making, though direct application to trading strategies is not demonstrated.

title: Specialized Large Language Models for Markovian Reasoning: Structural Cache Compression, Transition Pretraining, and Dual-Loop Transformers
summary: Standard autoregressive large language models attend to the growing history of generated tokens, making the key-value (KV) cache a central memory and throughput bottleneck in long-chain reasoning and multi-branch sampling. Yet an important class of reasoning problems is naturally first-order Markovian: the next step depends on a sufficient representation of the current state, rather than on the raw sequence of all earlier steps. We develop a unified design paradigm for Markovian-reasoning specialized large language models. At the cache level, the Markovian state interface transforms history-dependent KV storage into constant-size state transfer with respect to the number of reasoning steps. At the learning level, we reformulate long-chain prediction as independently trainable one-step transition objectives, with explicit state bottlenecks, distillation, invariance, and drift-consistency losses. At the architectural level, we introduce a dual-loop Transformer: an outer loop advances the reasoning state, while an inner recurrent-depth loop allocates adaptive computation to each transition through shared weights and explicit memory tokens or recurrent matrix states. We connect this architecture to a three-region cache, step-relative positions, truncated backpropagation, branch-aware checkpoints, and a transition-centric evaluation protocol. The organizing principle is simple: the optimal reasoning system need not remember everything; it must carry forward exactly what the future needs. This principle opens a path toward specialized reasoning engines whose memory footprint is decoupled from reasoning-chain length.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a specialized large language model (LLM) design for Markovian reasoning problems, focusing on state transfer, transition pretraining, and a dual-loop Transformer architecture to manage memory and computation efficiently.
data_sources: Not explicitly mentioned, but the methodology is applicable to sequential decision-making problems, which could include financial time series data.
alpha_potential: Limited direct alpha potential; however, the methodology could be adapted for Markovian processes in trading, such as short-term price prediction or order flow analysis.

title: TabK: Amortized Bayesian Estimation of the Number of Clusters in Tabular Data
summary: Estimating the number of clusters, $k$, is a fundamental prerequisite for most clustering algorithms. Traditionally, this estimation has relied on computationally expensive grid searches over internal cluster validity indices (CVIs) or adaptive clustering algorithms, both constrained by specific statistical assumptions. We introduce TabK, a zero-shot, permutation-invariant transformer architecture that frames the estimation of $k$ as an amortized Bayesian inference problem for tabular data. TabK leverages a novel Quantile Feature Encoder (QFE) to extract position-free, content-derived representations from empirical marginal distributions. By learning a generalized structural bias over a diverse synthetic prior, TabK estimates the number of clusters in a single forward pass per ensemble member. Evaluated across 50 diverse real-world benchmarks, TabK outperforms all competing methods, achieving a mean absolute error (MAE) value of 1.04 compared to 2.14 for the closest competitor. TabK also achieves the lowest average inference time, producing estimates in less than one second on average and running $2\times$ faster than TabClustPFN and $30\times$ faster than traditional CVIs such as Silhouette and Calinski-Harabasz. Code is available at https://github.com/mrbakhtyari/TabK.
core_methodology: Transformer architecture for estimating the number of clusters in tabular data using amortized Bayesian inference.
data_sources: Diverse synthetic prior data and 50 real-world benchmarks (unspecified financial relevance).
alpha_potential: Potential for improved clustering in feature engineering or market regime detection, but no direct trading application demonstrated.

title: Which Loans, Not How Many: Exactly Level-Invariant, Anytime-Valid Monitoring of Deployed Risk Models
summary: A refinancing wave can change the number of mortgage prepayments without changing the relationship between scores and prepayment. In a logistic model, conditioning on the monthly count removes the intercept from the likelihood of which loans prepay. Our fixed-start slope product tests a lower bound on the calibration slope. At threshold 20 its probability of ever crossing under the null is at most 5%. The restarted level sum tracks departures from intercept tolerance. A confidence sequence estimates a constant slope, and the restart-intersection rule detects changes in that slope. A continuous mixture avoids the off-grid width floor of a discrete prior. On Freddie Mac loans, fixed-slope resampling reproduces 78% of maintained-model monthly AUC variance in development and 70% in the holdout (95% intervals 57-100% and 48-100%). From fresh holdout starts, the restarted level sum crosses on both paths, and the fixed-start slope product stays below threshold on both. The restart-intersection rule signals a downward change for the frozen model in April 2018 and an upward change for the maintained model in a supplementary run in August 2019.
core_methodology: The paper introduces methods for monitoring risk models in mortgage prepayments, focusing on intercept removal in logistic models and tracking calibration slopes and intercept tolerances using fixed-start slope product tests and restarted level sums.
data_sources: Freddie Mac loan data
alpha_potential: The methodology could potentially be adapted for monitoring risk in other credit-related financial products, but its direct applicability to quantitative trading strategies is limited.

title: Two Actions from One State: Fork Futures Teach JEPA World Models to Compare
summary: JEPA world models are trained to predict logged transitions but used to compare counterfactual actions from one state. The logged behavior data show one action per state, and under a local linear approximation we prove the action response is unidentified along any direction the policy never varies within a state. We therefore supplement behavior data with measured outcomes of alternative actions from the same state. Our fork futures execute two actions from one restored state, and their outcome difference cancels the state term, identifying the action response on the sampled span. The resulting model, Fork-JEPA, matches predicted to measured differences, anchors the logged successor with behavior prediction, and adds a lookback head that keeps the predecessor recoverable, all at training time, leaving planning unchanged. On three visual control tasks, behavior-only training leaves the predicted action effect no better than a constant guess. Fork-JEPA makes it readable and raises planning success by up to 14\% over LeWM, its base model. Where the action response changes across hidden zones, it nearly doubles cross-zone success, and 1,024 fork pairs beat 1.2M extra behavior steps. Our project is available at https://fork-jepa.github.io/.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Fork-JEPA, a world model that uses fork futures to compare counterfactual actions from the same state, improving action response identification through measured outcomes of alternative actions.
data_sources: Behavior data from logged transitions and measured outcomes of alternative actions in visual control tasks.
alpha_potential: The methodology could potentially be adapted to compare different trading actions (e.g., buy vs. hold) from the same market state, but the paper focuses on visual control tasks, not financial markets.

title: Optimal User-Level Private Stochastic Convex Optimization and Mean Estimation with Heavy Tails
summary: We study stochastic convex optimization with heavy-tailed stochastic gradients under $(\varepsilon, \delta)$-user-level differential privacy, which protects each user's entire collection of samples. Instead of assuming a uniformly bounded Lipschitz constant, we only assume bounds on the second- and $k$-th moments of the random sample Lipschitz parameters. This allows for unbounded, heavy-tailed stochastic gradient distributions and can lead to sharper excess risk bounds. We characterize the minimax optimal excess population risk up to logarithmic factors. Our algorithm achieves the optimal rate with only $\widetilde{O}(1/\varepsilon)$ users. As a byproduct of our algorithmic developments, we obtain tight bounds for user-level private mean estimation under norm-moment assumptions, improving over the guarantees of Esfandiari et al. (2022) and Zhao et al. (2024). Finally, for mean estimation under the directional-moment assumption of Agarwal et al. (2025), we close their remaining approximate-DP gap by removing the additional $d/\varepsilon$ user requirement and attaining the optimal sample complexity up to logarithmic factors.
core_methodology: Stochastic convex optimization with heavy-tailed gradients under user-level differential privacy
data_sources: Not specified, likely synthetic or generic datasets
alpha_potential: Potential for robust optimization in private data settings, but unclear direct financial application

title: Information Access and Gain-Loss Framing in Six Large Language Models and Human Decision Makers
summary: A risky choice can be described by what will be saved or what will be lost, and people often choose differently depending on that wording. We test whether six large language models (LLMs) show this gain-loss framing effect, and whether it shrinks when they can first read more about the options. GPT-4.1, GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Qwen3 235B and Llama 4 Maverick made 11,519 choices across four risk scenarios, each in its original wording, two paraphrases and a mirrored version in the opposite wording. Before choosing, a model could open up to 0, 2, 3 or 4 of seven information cards. With no cards, all six models showed large framing effects: the share choosing the safe option was 27 to 79 percentage points lower under loss than under gain wording. The gap was smaller at 2 cards than with no cards in every model. Against a 10-point threshold set in our analysis plan, GPT-4.1 fell within it at 4 cards and Qwen3 only at 2 cards; in the plan's pooled comparison over all versions, GPT-4.1 was within it from 2 cards and GPT-4o from 3. GPT-4o-mini and Llama 4 Maverick kept gaps of 28 to 66 points with cards, and for GPT-4o-mini and Qwen3 the gap grew again from 2 to 4 cards. Part of the drop from 0 to 2 cards may reflect a change in prompt format, and most card content counted against the risky option, which may favor the safe choice. In an exploratory comparison with 198 students who saw the same scenarios and cards but opened cards one at a time and chose how many, decisions made after opening 0 or 1 cards showed a 19-point difference between the gain scenarios, asked first, and the loss scenarios, asked later, and no clear difference appeared in decisions made after opening more, though this design cannot show that cards reduced framing in people. With these cards, in the balanced comparison 17 of 18 card gaps were below the model's no-card gap, but few were within the threshold.
authors: Jeremy M. Gernand (The Pennsylvania State University)
core_methodology: The study examines the gain-loss framing effect in six large language models (LLMs) by testing their responses to risky choices under different wordings and information access levels.
data_sources: The research uses simulated risk scenarios and information cards to test LLM responses, with no real-world financial data involved.
alpha_potential: The study highlights potential biases in LLM decision-making under different framing effects, which could be relevant for understanding AI behavior in financial decision-making contexts, but does not directly suggest actionable trading strategies.

title: The Evaluation Substrate Matters: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Serving Substrates
summary: Multi-agent systems (MAS) usually coordinate heterogeneous models and tools to solve complex tasks, creating a growing need for reliable evaluation. However, a multi-agent workflow that is fastest in one serving environment can lose its advantage in another, even when its models, prompts, and task remain fixed. This makes a benchmark result conditional on how the workflow is executed. We introduce MASSys, a benchmark for measuring this dependence in multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems. MASSys executes the same candidate-task pairs across serving substrates and load regimes, using five workload families spanning software repair, research synthesis, financial analysis, interactive control, and diagram generation. It records task quality alongside delivery, latency, cost, resource pressure, and failure evidence. In a controlled motivation diagnostic, the Star workflow falls from first to fourth in mean-latency rank under KV-cache pressure, while Chain rises from fourth to first. The substrate sweeps further show that increasing load creates long runtime tails and timeout pressure. In several task families, quality among evaluated outputs changes less than effective quality over submitted jobs: the system delivers fewer usable results even when the surviving outputs remain competitive. Tool and runtime traces reveal that these outcomes involve both model serving and non-model execution. Together, the results motivate evaluating MAS designs over explicit operating conditions and reporting which tasks are delivered, how well they are solved, and where execution breaks down.
core_methodology: Benchmarking multi-agent LLM systems across different serving substrates to evaluate performance under varying conditions.
data_sources: Workload families including financial analysis, research synthesis, and other non-market-specific tasks.
alpha_potential: Limited direct alpha potential; focuses on system performance rather than financial predictions or strategies.

title: Beyond Invoice Volumes: Temporal Network Structure, Maturity Concentration, and Systemic Liquidity Exposure in SME Trade-Credit Networks
summary: Trade-credit invoices encode directed obligations whose temporal synchronization and counterparty concentration are obscured by annual volume totals. We audit 749,952 atomic B2B invoices from 2012-2023 (EUR 99.705B; 75,343 firms) from the pseudonymized Mendeley Data corpus (Esteva de la Rosa, 2026), separating 1,240 terminal 2024 bridge records (EUR 630.12M; 9 bridge-only firms) and 13 extreme-duration contracts (>3,650 days; EUR 297.75k). Using directed weighted graphs, HHI, Shannon entropy, CR1 shares, spectral centralities, and multi-cadence temporal operators, we formulate and benchmark a Maturity-Aware Network Exposure (MANE) indicator. Invoice values are heavily skewed: the top 1% hold 81.41% of value (Gini = 0.9742). Two-way fixed-effects panels with circular block bootstrapping ($B=999$, 12-month blocks) and Holm-Bonferroni control show higher lagged debtor counterparty concentration is associated with lower MANE ($\hat{\beta}=-0.494$, 95% CI $[-0.752,-0.248]$, $p_{\mathrm{Holm}}=0.004$). Robustness audits (R1-R4) confirm stability under 2021 exclusion ($-0.402$, $p=0.004$), Shannon entropy ($+0.257$), CR1 ($-0.515$), 1%-99% Winsorization ($-0.462$, all $p=0.001$), and multi-invoice debtors (count $\ge 2$, $-0.334$, $p=0.031$). Conversely, within-FE diagnostics expose severe joint-concentration multicollinearity (VIF = 22.22) that vanishes for multi-invoice debtors ($p=0.719$), while regime splits reveal a macro reciprocity sign reversal between 2012-2019 ($-0.706$) and 2020-2023 ($+0.232$, both $p=0.001$). In 12-month purged forecasting, MANE does not reliably improve over maturity seeds ($\Delta\mathrm{MSE}=2.668$, 95% CI $[-0.027,7.954]$; trimmed $0.067$, $[-0.035,0.194]$), positioning MANE as a reproducible screening and auditing diagnostic, rather than a default proxy, for supply-chain finance, multilateral clearing, and RWA tokenization.
core_methodology: Directed weighted graphs, HHI, Shannon entropy, spectral centralities, and multi-cadence temporal operators to formulate a Maturity-Aware Network Exposure (MANE) indicator.
data_sources: 749,952 atomic B2B invoices from 2012-2023 (EUR 99.705B; 75,343 firms) from the pseudonymized Mendeley Data corpus.
alpha_potential: Potential insights into systemic liquidity risk and counterparty concentration in SME trade-credit networks, but limited direct applicability to trading strategies.

title: STRIDE: Strategy-to-Tactics Retrieval-Guided Skill Disclosure and Evolution for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
summary: Skill-augmented reinforcement learning enables LLM agents to reuse task-solving knowledge across episodes, but existing systems typically expose agents to a flat skill pool and update skills only from coarse, episode-level outcomes. This conflates two distinct uses of experience: a stable strategy that should frame the whole episode, and tactical know-how that should be retrieved only when the agent reaches a local execution gap. We propose STRIDE (Strategy-to-Tactics Retrieval-guided skIll Disclosure and Evolution), a framework that brings progressive skill disclosure into agentic reinforcement learning. STRIDE keeps the selected strategy visible as episode context, exposes a compact tactic menu, and loads full tactic content only after an explicit retrieval action. This interface turns each retrieval into an event-level credit unit: the same event provides process feedback for learning when to retrieve and supplies evidence for skill-bank evolution. On ALFWorld, STRIDE achieves a 92.7% average success rate with Qwen3-4B and a 94.9% average success rate with Qwen3-8B. On WebShop, it improves over the strongest reproduced skill-augmented baseline by 4.5 score points and 1.9 success-rate percentage points. These results show that skill reuse is most effective when persistent strategies preserve global task structure and tactics are disclosed only at local decision bottlenecks.
core_methodology: Strategy-to-tactics retrieval-guided skill disclosure and evolution for reinforcement learning agents
data_sources: ALFWorld, WebShop (simulated environments, not financial data)
alpha_potential: Potential for developing hierarchical decision-making systems in algorithmic trading, though not directly demonstrated on financial data

title: Mirror Descent at the Edge of Stability
summary: In many deep learning settings, gradient descent has been shown to operate at the edge of stability -- a regime where the largest eigenvalue of the loss Hessian hovers around $2/\eta$. We study this phenomenon in mirror descent, a generalization of gradient descent. As mirror descent is non-Euclidean, existing explanations of the edge of stability phase do not extend to this setting. We generalize the existing notion of sharpness to introduce mirror sharpness, which measures the curvature of the loss with respect to the mirror potential. Empirically, we observe that the mirror sharpness hovers slightly above the $2/\eta$ threshold. Furthermore, we derive a dual central flow ODE for mirror descent that models iterates in continuous time at the onset of edge of stability. Our ODE provides insights into the difficulties of extending existing arguments for why sharpness stabilizes at $2/\eta$ from gradient descent to mirror descent in full generality.
core_methodology: Mirror descent, a generalization of gradient descent, analyzed at the edge of stability with mirror sharpness as a key metric.
data_sources: Theoretical study, no specific market data mentioned.
alpha_potential: Potential applications in optimizing trading strategies if adapted to specific financial contexts, but currently theoretical and lacks empirical validation in trading scenarios.

title: Dually Constrained Parameter Projection for Continual Learning
summary: Continual learning requires a model to learn multiple new tasks sequentially while retaining performance on previous tasks. Projecting model parameters onto the Jacobian null space of previous tasks after unconstrained training on a new task has emerged as an effective paradigm. However, unidirectional projection merely minimizes the parameter distance to the new-task optimum, overlooking the new-task loss landscape. To address this limitation, we propose DUET, a bidirectional projection algorithm that imposes Jacobian null-space constraints from both previous and new tasks during post-training projection. Specifically, DUET formulates the post-training adjustment as a dually constrained optimization problem. It minimizes the distance between parameters before and after training on a new task, subject to loss preserving constraints on both tasks. To solve the optimization problem, we develop an alternating bidirectional projection algorithm, whose convergence is guaranteed by the contraction mapping theorem. For reliable multi-step projection, we rectify existing step size selection criteria via an effective-rank aware formulation, overcoming their failure under rank-deficient Jacobians. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DUET consistently outperforms existing unidirectional projection methods and achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple datasets.
core_methodology: Bidirectional projection algorithm for continual learning that imposes Jacobian null-space constraints from both previous and new tasks during post-training projection.
data_sources: Not specified in the abstract, but typically involves multiple datasets for continual learning tasks in general machine learning contexts.
alpha_potential: Limited direct application to trading strategies, but could be adapted for sequential learning tasks in dynamic financial environments, such as evolving market regimes or factor models.

title: MoR4Rec: Mixture-of-Recursion for Sequential Recommendation
summary: Sequential recommender systems aim to predict a user's next interaction by modeling temporal dependencies in historical behavior sequences. To capture such dependencies, recent approaches increasingly rely on attention-based architectures, particularly transformers. While effective at modeling long-range sequential patterns, these models apply a fixed computation depth to all interaction items, treating them as equally complex. However, user behavior is inherently heterogeneous, with many interactions following simple repetitive patterns, whereas others require modeling higher-order dependencies. This mismatch leads to inefficient utilization of model capacity and unnecessary computational overhead, particularly in deep transformer-based architectures. To address this issue, we propose MoR4Rec, a sequential recommendation framework based on a Mixture-of-Recursion paradigm, which enables item-wise adaptive computation through a shared transformer backbone. A learned routing mechanism dynamically assigns each item to an appropriate recursion depth, allocating deeper computation to complex interactions while processing simpler patterns more efficiently. To improve computational efficiency, we develop a cascade-based strategy with key-value sharing across recursion steps. We further introduce a gated attention mechanism that adaptively regulates contextual information during recursive sequence modeling. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets show that MoR4Rec consistently outperforms strong transformer-based baselines, achieving average gains of 2.28% in Recall@5, 2.50% in NDCG@5, and 2.0% in MRR@5 over the strongest baseline. The improvements remain consistent across top-10 and top-20 recommendation cutoffs, while comparisons with vanilla transformers demonstrate the computational efficiency of adaptive recursive processing.
core_methodology: Mixture-of-Recursion (MoR) for adaptive computation in sequential recommendation
data_sources: User behavior sequences in recommendation systems
alpha_potential: Potential to model heterogeneous user behaviors more efficiently, though not directly applicable to financial data without significant adaptation

title: Learning-Augmented QUBO for Time-Expanded Multi-Commodity Flow
summary: We study energy-aware multi-commodity flow on time-expanded graphs, a problem that captures dynamic routing in layered networks and is NP-hard in general. We formulate the problem as a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization problem, give an explicit penalty coefficient that provably guarantees feasibility, and show that it is smaller than the standard bound by a factor of roughly the number of active links. The layered structure of the time-expanded graph yields three structural results: a treewidth bound that gives a fixed-parameter tractable exact algorithm in the bag size, a matrix-product-operator representation of small bond dimension, and a proof that the annealing gap of the associated Ising Hamiltonian is strictly positive for every instance with a unique optimum, uniformly over bounded windows. For learning-augmented routing, we bound the Hamming distance between a predicted and an optimal flow by the flow error, and prove a consistency guarantee: a hybrid algorithm that keeps the better of the prediction and the solver output returns a flow whose cost exceeds the optimum by a factor that grows linearly with the prediction error. The results are exact statements about the QUBO and its associated Ising Hamiltonian, and they hold for any physical implementation.
core_methodology: Quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) applied to time-expanded multi-commodity flow problems, with learning-augmented routing for hybrid solutions.
data_sources: Theoretical network models (time-expanded graphs) without specific market data.
alpha_potential: Limited direct financial application, though optimization techniques could potentially be adapted for routing problems in high-frequency trading or order execution.

title: Randomized Weighted Distance Nearest Neighbor Classification
summary: The nearest neighbor classifier is known to be memory-inefficient, and a popular solution is to compress its training data. Recently, a compression algorithm based on weighted distance nearest neighbor (WNN) was proposed, which has elegant theoretical properties and effective classification performance. However, its compression process is computationally expensive, for it performs a greedy search of the densest homogeneous balls in data space. In this paper, we propose a randomized variant RWNN. It simply randomizes the ball search process, and results in substantially reduced compression time (often 0.1%--1% of WNN's) and similar classification accuracy. RWNN also inherits several theoretical properties of WNN including consistency and a generalization bound. Experimental results on multiple datasets demonstrate its efficacy.
core_methodology: Randomized variant of weighted distance nearest neighbor classification (WNN) that speeds up compression time while maintaining similar accuracy.
data_sources: Generic classification datasets (not financial-specific).
alpha_potential: Limited direct application in trading; may help in improving efficiency of nearest neighbor-based classification tasks in finance, but unclear signal generation mechanism.

title: Dimension Is Free, Horizon Is Not: When Evolution Strategies Rival Policy Gradients for LLM Fine-Tuning
